title: Case Report: Two cases of HELLP-syndrome-associated hepatic subcapsular hematoma and rupture: distinct phenotypes, multidisciplinary management, and subsequent-pregnancy follow-up
abstract: Background Hepatic subcapsular hematoma and rupture represents a rare and highly lethal complication of HELLP syndrome. Limited systematic clinical data exists regarding its disease spectrum, pathophysiology, therapeutic dilemmas, and long-term subsequent-pregnancy outcomes among survivors. Case presentation Case 1 involved a 32-year-old woman with severe preeclampsia who developed an antenatal hepatic subcapsular hematoma with focal capsular defects at 28 +6 weeks of gestation. At admission, she did not meet complete HELLP criteria; postoperatively, she developed hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes and thrombocytopenia, reaching Mississippi Class 1 HELLP. After initial surgical hemostasis, she developed persistent hematoma extension and extensive inferior vena cava–iliac venous thrombosis. Multidisciplinary management included enoxaparin for 9 days followed by rivaroxaban and image-guided hematoma drainage. In a subsequent pregnancy, she developed gestational hypertension without reported recurrence of hepatic injury. The index neonate weighed 990 g, with Apgar scores 0/2/3, and died shortly after delivery. Case 2 involved a 39-year-old woman who developed postpartum eclampsia followed by extensive hepatic capsular avulsion and massive intra-abdominal hemorrhage after precipitous out-of-hospital delivery at 36 +3 weeks. Acute-phase testing showed hypoglycemia, hyperammonemia, elevated bilirubin and low fibrinogen; Swansea criteria were fulfilled (≥8 items), so AFLP could not be excluded. Damage-control surgery, massive transfusion, renal replacement therapy, and other critical-care interventions were required. Pregnancy-associated atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome was considered but not confirmed. She was discharged after 41 days of hospitalization and subsequently showed substantial clinical and biochemical recovery. The infant weighed 1880g and was discharged alive. Conclusions These cases illustrate distinct patterns of HELLP-associated hepatic injury, from a subcapsular hematoma with partial focal defects of the hepatic capsule to catastrophic hepatic rupture. Early recognition, bleeding control tailored to the clinical presentation, and multidisciplinary management are central to care. Follow-up should address thrombotic complications, organ recovery, and hypertensive disorders in subsequent pregnancies.

title: Measuring care coordination for people with multiple long-term conditions using electronic health records: a scoping review
abstract: Care coordination is essential to high-quality care for people living with multiple long-term conditions (MLTC), yet no standardised measure of coordination derivable from electronic health records (EHRs) exists for assessing care quality. This scoping review identified and mapped measures of care coordination and relational continuity applicable to routinely collected electronic health data and assessed their relevance to people living with MLTC. Following Joanna Briggs Institute methodology, we searched MEDLINE, EMBASE, CINAHL, PsycINFO and Scopus to February 2025, supplemented by grey literature searching and citation chasing. Titles and abstracts were dual-screened, and records applying existing measures were keyword-triaged for derivability from routinely collected data. Eligible measures were charted and mapped to the domains of the Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality Care Coordination Atlas and to relational continuity, with each mapping classified as direct or indirect. Searches identified 7,074 records; 38 studies met the inclusion criteria, contributing 64 unique measures. Studies were predominantly US-based and used claims or population-level data; only two focused specifically on people with MLTC. Measures clustered around accountability, monitoring and follow-up, and relational continuity. No measure captured proactive care planning or linkage with community resources, and only two addressed support for self-management. Of 137 measure-to-domain mappings, 93 (68%) were indirect, inferring coordination from patterns of contact. Routine electronic data record the observable traces of coordination more readily than its anticipatory, relational and person-centred aspects. Population-level evaluation is likely to require a small suite of complementary routine-data indicators, interpreted alongside patient-reported measures; no single indicator will suffice.

title: Outcomes of trial of labor after two cesarean deliveries: a single-center retrospective cohort study
journal: The Journal of Maternal-Fetal & Neonatal Medicine
abstract: BACKGROUND: The global rise in cesarean delivery (CD) rates has led to an increasing number of women with multiple prior CDs. Despite growing evidence in support of trial of labor after two CD (TOLA2C), its adoption remains limited in many settings owing to concerns regarding potential complications, particularly uterine rupture. This study aimed to compare maternal and neonatal outcomes between trial of labor after two cesarean sections (TOLA2C) and elective repeat cesarean delivery (ERCD) within a single institution and to characterize maternal and obstetric features among women with successful and failed TOLA2C. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 333 women with two or more previous CDs who gave birth between January 2021 and December 2023. Women with multiple pregnancies were excluded. Patients were categorized according to the intended mode of delivery into ERCD and TOLA2C groups. Maternal characteristics, birth outcomes, and complications were extracted from digital medical records. Continuous variables were summarized using means with standard deviations and medians with interquartile ranges, and categorical variables as frequencies and percentages. Group comparisons were performed using the Wilcoxon-Mann-Whitney test, Welch's two-sample t-test, chi-square test, or Fisher's exact test, as appropriate. A p value <0.05 was considered statistically significant. RESULTS: In total, 333 women met the eligibility criteria for the study. Among them, 295 (88.6%) underwent ERCD, whereas 38 (11.4%) attempted TOLA2C. The success rate of TOLA2C was 60.5% (23/38), whereas 39.5% (15/38) required an unplanned CD. Uterine scar dehiscence was identified in one woman undergoing TOLA2C (2.6%) and in 10 women undergoing ERCD (3.4%), whereas complete uterine rupture occurred in one woman with schedulded ERCD (0.3%). No uterine scar event was associated with maternal or neonatal death. No maternal deaths or embolic events were reported, one hysterectomy and one case of intrauterine infection occurred. Overall, there were no significant differences in maternal or neonatal complications between the two groups. CONCLUSION: Among women with two prior cesarean deliveries in our study population, TOLA2C resulted in vaginal birth in 60.5% of attempts. No statistically significant differences in the evaluated maternal and neonatal complications were detected between TOLA2C and ERCD; however, the small TOLA2C sample and potential selection bias preclude conclusions regarding equivalence or comparative safety. TOLA2C may be considered in appropriately selected women following individualized counseling in adequately equipped obstetric centers.

title: Impact of slit versus non-slit mesh on recurrence after inguinal hernia repair: a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Background Inguinal hernia repair is among the most frequently performed operations worldwide, and durable mesh-based repair is the standard of care. During laparo-endoscopic repair, surgeons choose between slit and non-slit mesh to accommodate the cord structures, yet the optimal configuration remains uncertain. We aimed to determine whether slit mesh, compared with non-slit mesh, reduces recurrence without increasing chronic groin pain or mesh-related complications. Methods We searched Embase, PubMed and Scopus for comparative studies of slit versus non-slit mesh in adults undergoing inguinal hernia repair. Randomised controlled trials and prospective or retrospective comparative cohorts were eligible. Two reviewers independently screened records, extracted data and assessed risk of bias using Cochrane RoB-2 and the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale, with certainty rated using GRADE. Dichotomous outcomes were pooled as odds ratios (OR) and continuous outcomes as mean differences (MD), using random-effects models with restricted maximum likelihood (REML) estimation as the primary analysis. Sensitivity analyses used the DerSimonian-Laird and Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman (HKSJ) estimators, the latter recommended when few studies contribute to an outcome. Recurrence was also analysed by study design, by leave-one-out analysis and using adjusted effect estimates where available. Heterogeneity was quantified with the I2 statistic. Results Six comparative studies were included: one quasi-randomised trial and five retrospective cohorts. The trial reported no recurrence in either arm, so five studies (3,825 hernias or patients) contributed to the pooled recurrence estimate. In the primary REML analysis, slit mesh was associated with lower recurrence (OR 0.43, 95% CI 0.20 to 0.91; P = 0.028; I2 = 33.5%). This finding was not robust. With the HKSJ adjustment the interval was 0.14 to 1.32 (P = 0.105), and the 95% prediction interval was 0.06 to 3.11. Omitting Chue et al. (OR 0.47, 95% CI 0.16 to 1.39) or Zarras et al. (OR 0.48, 95% CI 0.16 to 1.46) removed statistical significance. The association was confined to these two propensity-adjusted or matched cohorts, which had the shortest follow-up (OR 0.33, 95% CI 0.16 to 0.67), and was absent in the three unadjusted cohorts (OR 0.55, 95% CI 0.10 to 3.08). Chronic pain (5 studies; OR 1.42, 95% CI 0.96 to 2.10; P = 0.080), operative time and length of stay did not differ significantly. Certainty of evidence was very low for all outcomes. Conclusions The evidence is very uncertain about the effect of slit mesh on recurrence compared with non-slit mesh. The point estimate favoured slit mesh, but the association depends on two observational cohorts with short follow-up and does not persist under HKSJ estimation. Its plausible range is compatible with both a substantial reduction and an increase in recurrence. The evidence is also very uncertain about the effect of slit mesh on chronic pain, and a modest increase in chronic pain cannot be excluded. This evidence does not support overturning existing international guideline caution against routine mesh slitting. Adequately powered randomised data with standardised slit technique and longer follow-up are needed before either configuration can be recommended over the other.

title: Flexible surge capacity as a health system governance strategy in disasters: a scoping review of EMT and NGO integration
abstract: Background The increasing frequency and complexity of disasters place substantial pressure on health systems and frequently exceed routine healthcare service capacity. Traditional surge capacity, commonly conceptualized through the four components of staff, supplies, structure/space, and systems, is often insufficient to ensure continuity and quality of care during large-scale or prolonged emergencies. Flexible Surge Capacity (FSC) extends this approach by enabling health systems to mobilize community resources, alternative care settings, and non-state actors. Emergency Medical Teams (EMTs) and Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs) represent critical service delivery partners within FSC, yet their integration into national health services remains variable and poorly synthesized. Objective This scoping review aims to synthesize evidence on the roles of EMTs and NGOs in supporting health service surge capacity, with a particular focus on integration mechanisms, enabling and constraining factors, and implications for health system organization and performance within FSC frameworks. Methods The review followed Arksey and O’Malley’s methodological framework and the PRISMA-ScR reporting guidelines. Searches were conducted in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar for studies published between 2005 and 2025. Eighteen studies met the inclusion criteria. Data were analyzed using a combination of deductive and inductive thematic analysis supported by NVivo, informed by the WHO surge capacity (4S) model and FSC principles. Results EMTs primarily contributed deployable clinical services that expanded health workforce and facility capacity in trauma, burn, infectious disease, and sudden-impact disaster contexts. NGOs supported service continuity through flexible logistics, community engagement, and sustained recovery-oriented care. Effective integration into health service delivery was observed where clear governance arrangements, established command and coordination structures, regional healthcare coalitions, and FSC-enabled community service platforms were present. Persistent barriers included fragmented service coordination, misaligned clinical and operational protocols, workforce and logistics constraints, and weak integration with routine health system processes. Conclusion EMTs and NGOs play essential roles in maintaining and extending healthcare service delivery during disasters. FSC provides a practical health systems framework for integrating external responders with national and community-based services. Strengthening FSC-related governance and coordination mechanisms is critical for improving surge capacity, continuity of care, and health system resilience in future emergencies.

title: The Economic Value of Crisis Communication in Digital Healthcare Emergencies: Spokesperson Structures, Trust, and Information Governance
journal: International Journal of Online and Biomedical Engineering (iJOE)
abstract: The ability to communicate effectively during an emergency is critical when organizations rely on digital technologies. This study analyzes the economic value of crisis communication in digitally-based healthcare environments and focuses specifically upon: (1) the structural arrangements of spokespeople within organizations; (2) institutional trustworthiness; and (3) governance of data/information. Effective crisis communication is best viewed as an essential aspect of a resilient healthcare system rather than simply as an external function of public relations. Building upon literature in the areas of crisis communication, public administration, health governance, and digital health implementation, this study establishes a theoretical model connecting communication capacity to economic resilience outcomes in healthcare emergencies. This paper develops a conceptual model showing how open communication practices, clearly defined spokesperson roles, and coordinated information governance can support stakeholder confidence and improve decision-making efficiency during digital healthcare emergencies.

title: Incidences of suicide and unintentional poisoning mortality after discharge from involuntary psychiatric hospitalization
abstract: Aims Approximately 1 million involuntary psychiatric hospitalizations (IPHs) occur annually in the United States, but post-discharge outcomes are understudied. This study sought to characterize incidences of suicide and unintentional poisoning death following IPH and investigate factors associated with these outcomes. Methods Using data from the New Opportunities for Health and Resilience Measures for Suicide Prevention project, this population-based retrospective cohort study included all people with ≥1 IPH initiated in King County, Washington, from 2016 to 2022 (N = 22,104). IPH records were linked to state death records. Crude cumulative incidences and incidence rates of suicide and unintentional poisoning mortality after discharge were estimated. Cox regressions were used to investigate associations with sociodemographic and clinical variables. Results The median age was 37 years (interquartile range: 27–53) at most recent IPH; 55.5% of participants were men, and the mean follow-up time was 2.49 years. The 1-month rates of suicide and unintentional poisoning were 1,180.6 and 2,192.5 per 100,000 person-years, respectively, compared with rates of 173.0 and 402.0 per 100,000 person-years from 1 to 7 years post-discharge (incidence rate ratio suicide [IRR] = 6.82; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 4.20–11.08; IRR poisoning = 5.45; 95% CI: 3.85–7.72). The 30-day and 1-year cumulative incidences were 0.10% (95% CI: 0.06–0.15%) and 0.57% (95% CI: 0.47–0.68%) for suicide and 0.18% (95% CI: 0.13–0.24%) and 0.91% (95% CI: 0.79–1.05%) for unintentional poisoning. Suicide by suffocation or hanging was more common than other suicide methods, including firearms. A Danger-to-Self detention order was significantly associated with the rates of suicide (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] = 2.20, 95% CI: 1.42–3.43) and unintentional poisoning mortality (aHR = 1.44, 95% CI: 1.06–1.96) compared to a Danger-to-Others order. Conclusions The suicide and unintentional poisoning mortality rates in this study underscore the importance of improving post-discharge care for people who undergo IPH, as a critical period of heightened risk was seen in the first month and year after discharge. Improved transition to post-discharge care, preventive measures such as means restriction, and substance use interventions represent opportunities for future study. Further research is needed to understand the effects of policies and healthcare practices on risks of mortality and other adverse events after IPH, and the possibility that IPHs entail iatrogenic harm, so that reliable recommendations to reduce mortality from suicide and unintentional poisoning can be developed for clinicians and policymakers.

title: In their own voices: exploring language barriers in mental health care among Mandarin Chinese-speaking service users and their supporters in Germany
abstract: Background Individuals who prefer a language other than a country’s official or commonly spoken one(s) often encounter various barriers when accessing mental healthcare services. This study aimed to explore the experiences of first-generation Mandarin Chinese-speaking migrant service users in Germany, focusing on language-related challenges and their attitudes toward various strategies for overcoming them, including using qualified interpreters, informal interpreters (i.e., multilingual (mental) healthcare personnel or relatives/friends), and technological tools. Methods Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 10 Mandarin Chinese-speaking service users (SUs) and three supporters (SuPs) (i.e., individuals who help service users access mental healthcare services). The interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim and analyzed using a structuring qualitative content analysis approach, combining inductive and deductive coding. Results Participants were predominantly female (n = 8 female SUs, n = 3 female SuPs) and young (M SU = 30 years and M SuP = 29). Among the SUs, all were highly educated (i.e., Bachelor’s degree or higher) and had an average length of residence in Germany of 5 years. Service users reported that language disparities and communicating in a different language than their first language led to cognitive challenges, such as the pressure of processing emotions while translating and a tendency to overthink. Feelings of being ignored and difficulties clarifying uncertainties hindered the development of a trusting therapeutic relationship. Additionally, cultural (e.g., stress of explaining cultural contexts) and structural barriers (e.g., difficulties in navigating the local healthcare system and limited therapist availability) further compounded the challenges. However, multilingual interactions with their mental healthcare providers also brought several benefits, including improved communication competence. General concerns were raised regarding the presence of a third party in a therapy setting, e.g., extended session durations and potential information loss. Specific concerns and advantages were expressed regarding the use of qualified interpreters (e.g., balancing empathy and neutrality), informal interpreters such as relatives or friends (e.g., emotional support and confidentiality issues) and technological tools (e.g., emotional nuance challenges and feeling less judged due to their objectivity and neutrality). Conclusion This study provides insights into the variety and complexity of language-related and cultural challenges Mandarin Chinese-speaking migrants face when accessing mental healthcare in Germany and highlights the importance of flexible and person-centered approaches to deal with language barriers, including increased accessibility and utilization of qualified interpreters. However, most participants in this study were female, young and highly educated. Future studies should include more diverse Mandarin Chinese-speaking migrants, e.g., in terms of age, gender, educational background and years of residency.

title: An integrated blockchain and large language model decision support system for organ donation and transplantation workflows
abstract: Introduction Each donated organ creates an urgent coordination challenge because clinical evidence, allocation priorities, and institutional approvals must be brought together quickly, securely, and transparently. Existing approaches support parts of this process, but ranking, information review, record protection, and workflow governance remain separate. This fragmentation obscures how evidence informs a recommendation and the authorized actions that follow. Methods We present an integrated blockchain and large language model (LLM) decision support system connecting transparent ranking, constrained note review, deterministic safeguards, encrypted records, and authorized workflow actions. Structured attributes establish organ-specific reference rankings. The LLM only assigns predefined readiness states from notes, receives no rank information, and cannot select recipients. The safeguard excludes candidates on temporary hold and preserves the order of those remaining, while smart contracts govern the workflow. We evaluated the system using a synthetic dataset informed by public organ allocation guidance and clinically relevant compatibility, urgency, logistics, and readiness factors. The dataset comprised 1,600 training, 320 validation, and 400 independent test cases balanced across kidney, liver, heart, and lung workflows. Results Fine-tuned Qwen and GPT-4o mini returned valid and complete outputs in 93.0% and 97.0% of cases, with macro F1 scores of 99.3% and 99.6% among valid and complete outputs, respectively. When every candidate in an unsuccessful case was counted as incorrectly classified, the corresponding overall macro F1 scores were 95.3% and 98.0%. The selected primary recipient agreed with the synthetic reference in 372 and 387 cases, respectively. In a post hoc robustness analysis, all 20 scenarios produced the expected selection or stopped safely without creating a decision. A complete demonstration on the Sepolia blockchain test network executed all 45 transactions successfully using 6,932,168 gas; across 30 repetitions, the decision process had a median duration of 37.46 s. All 41 smart contract tests passed, and static security analysis with Slither reported no findings across 102 detectors. Discussion These results demonstrate the technical feasibility of integrating constrained LLM note review with transparent allocation logic and accountable workflow governance under controlled synthetic conditions. The system provides a reproducible foundation for further evaluation with clinical records and prospective assessment of clinical effectiveness.

title: Chronically Implantable Low‐Loss Soft Waveguides for Optogenetic Seizure Suppression in Rodents
abstract: Optical neuromodulation is a promising approach for next‐generation therapies targeting neurological disorders. However, clinical translation requires efficient and safe delivery of light to deep brain regions. Conventional solutions used in preclinical studies rely on implantable silica fibers or implantable light sources; however, such stiff implants may exacerbate foreign body responses or generate heat. In contrast, using soft and flexible materials improves tissue compliance but often compromises optical performance and require shuttles or bioresorbable coatings for implantation. To overcome these limitations, a waveguide‐based neural probe was developed, fabricated from highly transparent, microfabrication‐compatible materials balancing optical efficiency with mechanical compliance. The multimode waveguides exhibit propagation losses below 0.30 dB between = 450 and 700 nm, while single‐mode waveguides show losses of 0.37–0.41 dB across = 488–638 nm. Fabricated from materials with a Young's modulus of approximately 1 GPa, the waveguides provide sufficient stiffness for insertion while maintaining flexibility. Mechanical properties, stability, and implantability were evaluated ex vivo and in vivo in rodents. Biocompatibility was confirmed according to ISO 10993 standards. The waveguides were successfully implanted, and tissue response was assessed using immunohistochemistry after implantation in rats for 6 weeks. Finally, successful optogenetic suppression of experimental seizures was obtained in rats.

title: Enhancing classification performance on medical datasets using multi-layer perceptron-based feature ranking
abstract: Machine learning (ML) models aim to train on valuable data, where this data is passed through different preprocessing steps. The feature selection methods eliminate irrelevant features, simplify the model, and enhance its generalization. All these aspects effectively improve the model performance, thereby improving the accuracy. Accordingly, the feature selection methodologies are able to enrich the ML models, especially in the medical applications, where balancing performance and efficiency is very essential. Multi-layer perceptron (MLP) is the most common type of neural network that attempts to simulate biological neural networks’ functions. This paper proposes an MLP model as a feature selection strategy to determine the most relevant and significant features for medical datasets. More deeply, this MLP structure uses a bottleneck architecture with geometrically reduced hidden layers, which ensures progressive information compression and improves generalization to ensure a principled and interpretable architecture. The proposed MLP model determines the best subsets (k) of the features based on their accuracy to improve the classification performance. Thereafter, the required time for each (k) value is computed to specify the computational costs. Furthermore, other different classic feature selection methods are implemented, which are Chi-square (chi²), Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE), Wrapper, Mutual Information (MI), and Variance thresholding methods. To evaluate the proposed MLP model, Breast Cancer Wisconsin (BCW), Cervical cancer, Parkinson’s, and Prostate cancer datasets are used. The current MLP model achieved an accuracy of 98.25%, 98.26%, 96.61%, and 96.77% for these datasets, respectively. According to these results, the MLP-based method not only delivered superior performance but also provided interpretable, weight-derived feature rankings through determining some features as highly weighted features, aligning with clinical relevance. This work illustrates that MLPs can serve as both high-performance classifiers and intrinsic feature selectors, presenting a powerful, interpretable, and competitive alternative method to traditional ones in medical diagnostic modeling, besides allowing for more informed clinical decisions.

title: Factors associated with delayed emergency evaluation among high-acuity patients in a Ugandan tertiary Emergency Department: a cross-sectional study
abstract: Introduction Delayed clinical assessment compromises outcomes for high-acuity emergency patients. We assessed the prevalence and factors associated with delayed door-to-doctor time (DDT) among high-acuity patients at a tertiary referral hospital in South-Western Uganda. Methods This prospective, cross-sectional observational study was conducted between April and June 2025 at Mbarara Regional Referral Hospital. High-acuity patients (red and yellow categories according to the Uganda Triage and Treatment algorithm) were sampled. Delayed DDT was defined as >10 min for red and >60 min for yellow patients. Multivariable logistic regression identified independent predictors of delay. Results Out of 432 participants (median age 43 years, 62.3% male), 49.1% (95% CI: 44.4–53.8; n = 212) experienced delayed DDT. Delays were higher in red category patients than yellow (57.9%vs 46.2%). Prolonged DDT was significantly associated with clinical assessment on the medical side of the ED (AOR = 2.22, 95% CI: 1.25–3.95), lack of formal triage nurse handover (AOR = 1.71, 95% CI: 1.07–2.73), and departmental bed occupancy ≥ 100% at triage (AOR = 1.76, 95% CI: 1.15–2.69). Conversely, age ≤ 17 years was associated with reduced odds of delay (AOR = 0.41, 95% CI: 0.18–0.92). Conclusion Nearly half of high-acuity emergency presentations missed standard national evaluation windows. Structural interventions targeting spatial configurations, mandatory nurse- to-physician handovers, and active surge management are crucial to improve emergency care timelines in low-resource settings.

title: Research on the Influencing Factors of Power Battery Range Degradation and Optimization Strategies
journal: International Journal of Science and Engineering Applications

title: Enhanced recovery after surgery, based perioperative bundle reduces 30-day unplanned readmission after laparoscopic colorectal cancer surgery
abstract: BACKGROUND Laparoscopic resection has become standard for colorectal cancer (CRC) but postoperative recovery is often impaired by delayed gastrointestinal function, poor mobility and inadequate pain control resulting in increased risk of complications and unplanned readmission. Recovery is generally slower with conventional care, which follows conservative feeding and activity protocols. Enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS) pathway combines several evidence-based perioperative interventions that reduce surgical stress and promote recovery, but there are no specific data regarding the effect of this program on 30-day unplanned readmission after laparoscopic colonoctol cancer surgery. This study was designed to compare an ERAS-based perioperative bundle with conventional care in terms of 30-day unplanned readmission and recovery outcomes. AIM To analyze the impact of ERAS pathway-based comprehensive perioperative management bundle on 30-day unplanned readmission rate after laparoscopic radical resection for CRC, and to evaluate its improvement effects on patients’ recovery-related indicators, functional recovery, and quality of life. METHODS We retrospectively analyzed 77 patients underwent laparoscopic radical resection for CRC in the Department of Gastrointestinal Surgery of our hospital from July 2020 to June 2021. Patients were divided based on the initiation time of rehabilitation treatment protocols: Control group (n = 38, conventional rehabilitation care) and intervention group (n = 39, ERAS pathway-based comprehensive perioperative management bundle). The intervention group received a combination of preoperative individualized rehabilitation education, postoperative early activity training, gastrointestinal function rehabilitation, multimodal analgesia, psychological support and discharge preparation with continuity of care as multilateral comprehensive managementiy. The unplanned 30-day readmission rate, recovery-related indicators, pain scores, functional recovery indicators, satisfaction with treatment and quality of life were compared between the groups. RESULTS The 30-day unplanned readmission rate in the intervention group (5.1%) was significantly lower than that recorded in controls (23.7%) (Fisher’s exact test, P = 0.024). Compared with the control group, time to first ambulation, first flatus, first defecation and recovery of gastrointestinal function in intervention group were shorter (all P < 0.001). Patients in the intervention group had significantly lower pain scores than those in the control group on postoperative days 1, 3, and 7 (all P < 0.001). In the intervention group, the 6-minute walk distance on postoperative day 7 was significantly greater than that in the control group (P < 0.001). Barthel Index scores at discharge and 30 days postoperatively in the intervention group were superior to those of the control group (P < 0.05). At 30 days postoperatively, the patient satisfaction scores in the intervention group were significantly higher than the controls (P < 0.001), and all dimensions of 36-item short-form health survey quality of life scale showed various degrees of improvement at 30-day after surgery (P < 0.05). CONCLUSION The ERAS pathway-based comprehensive perioperative management bundle can reduce the 30-day unplanned readmission rate after laparoscopic CRC surgery significantly, which in effectively promotes early postoperative recovery, pain control, functional recovery level and improves quality of life. In summary, the synergistic effects of each individual component are attributed to these clinical advantages because the intervention is a multi-component bundle and worthy of clinical perioperative care promotion and application.

title: Inflammatory cloacogenic polyp of the rectum in a 16-year-old female: a case report
abstract: Background Inflammatory cloacogenic polyp (ICP) is a rare benign lesion of the anorectal transitional zone, typically affecting adults between the fourth and sixth decades of life. Its endoscopic appearance may mimic neoplasia, and reports in adolescents are exceedingly scarce. Case presentation A 16‑year‑old female presented with a one‑month history of intermittent fresh rectal bleeding. Digital rectal examination revealed two firm submucosal masses approximately 1 cm from the anal verge. Colonoscopy identified two broad‑based lobulated lesions at the anorectal junction with surrounding mucosal congestion and superficial ulceration. Targeted biopsies showed only chronic inflammation with granulation tissue, and a clinical diagnosis of rectal tumour could not be excluded. Transanal local excision was performed under spinal anaesthesia using ultrasonic shears, with primary closure of the wound beds. Final histopathology confirmed inflammatory cloacogenic polyp, with no dysplasia or malignancy. The patient resumed oral intake on the same day and was discharged on postoperative day 2 without complications. Follow‑up colonoscopy was scheduled at 3 to 6 months. Conclusions ICP should be considered in the differential diagnosis of rectal bleeding and polypoid lesions in adolescents, even when the clinical impression favours neoplasia. Transanal excision provides definitive diagnosis and treatment in a single procedure, with favourable short‑term outcomes.

title: Acute kidney injury after liver cancer ablation: Risk factors and perioperative management
abstract: BACKGROUND Evidence regarding the risk factors for and clinical management of acute kidney injury (AKI) following liver cancer (LC) ablation remains limited. AIM To investigate the incidence and potential risk factors for AKI following LC ablation and explore relevant clinical preventive strategies. METHODS This retrospective study included 168 patients with LC who underwent ablation between May 2022 and February 2026. Patients were classified into AKI (n = 25) and non-AKI (n = 143) groups according to postoperative AKI occurrence. Baseline characteristics, tumor-related characteristics (laterality, TNM stage, tumor size, tumor number, and ablation type), and laboratory parameters were compared between groups. Univariate and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify factors associated with AKI after LC ablation. RESULTS Age, diabetes, TNM stage, tumor size, hemoglobin (Hb), uric acid (UA), and serum creatinine (SCr) differed significantly between groups. Univariate analysis identified older age, diabetes, larger tumor size, higher UA, and higher SCr levels as potential risk factors, while higher Hb was associated with a lower risk of AKI. Multivariate analysis identified Hb and SCr as independent factors associated with AKI, with higher Hb associated with a lower risk [odds ratio (OR): 0.908, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.867-0.950, P < 0.001] and higher SCr associated with an increased risk (OR: 1.040, 95%CI: 1.004-1.078, P = 0.031). CONCLUSION Lower preoperative Hb and higher preoperative SCr levels may increase the risk of AKI after LC ablation. Preoperative anemia management and renal function assessment may help identify high-risk patients and guide individualized perioperative renal protection strategies.

title: Acquired hemophilia A following choledochal cyst excision - highlighting postoperative bile leak and infection as potential triggers: A case report
abstract: BACKGROUND Acquired hemophilia A (AHA) is a rare and potentially fatal bleeding disorder mediated by autoantibodies against coagulation factor VIII (FVIII). Its nonspecific clinical presentation often leads to delayed diagnosis and life-threatening complications. Early recognition and standardized management are crucial for improving outcomes. Secondary AHA following choledochal cyst excision is extremely rare, with no prior reports in the literature. This case report explored the possible etiology, treatment strategies, and disease course of AHA in a patient. CASE SUMMARY A 37-year-old woman developed postoperative bile leakage, infection, and recurrent bleeding after laparoscopic choledochal cyst excision with Roux-en-Y hepaticojejunostomy, which was subsequently complicated by AHA. On postoperative day 6, she presented with intra-abdominal hemorrhage. Despite repeated interventions, including exploratory laparotomy and interventional embolization, intermittent active bleeding remained uncontrolled. After multidisciplinary team consultation, she was finally diagnosed with AHA. Treatment included infection control, combined immunosuppressive therapy with corticosteroids and cyclophosphamide, seven plasma exchange sessions, and FVIII replacement therapy. Bleeding was effectively controlled, the intra-abdominal abscess healed, and the patient was discharged after clinical remission was achieved. At the 6-month follow-up, no signs of recurrent bleeding were noted. CONCLUSION Prompt FVIII activity and inhibitor testing, along with comprehensive treatment, should be implemented in patients suspicious for AHA.

title: Neurofilament light dynamics in critically ill COVID-19 ARDS patients
abstract: Neurological assessment in the intensive care unit (ICU) may benefit from blood-based neurobiomarkers. Neurofilament light (NfL) reflects neuroaxonal injury, but its dynamics in acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) are poorly characterised, limiting interpretation of raised levels. In a single-centre cohort of 116 invasively ventilated severe COVID-19 ARDS patients (611 serial plasma NfL samples, median 5 per patient), we modelled the four-week trajectory using linear mixed models, testing whether peak NfL predicted one-year mortality before and after adjustment for age and creatinine, and whether NfL at extubation or discharge approximated peak NfL. Peak NfL was associated with mortality but lost significance after adjustment for age and creatinine, with modest discrimination (AUC 0.61 alone). NfL rose throughout admission, stabilising around day 16 (survivors) and day 21 (non-survivors) and reaching 5–8 standard deviations above age-specific reference values; levels at extubation and discharge approximated peak values in most patients. NfL was not clearly altered by stroke or dialysis in a case series. After accounting for age and renal function, NfL did not independently predict mortality. However it could be regarded as a marker of neuroaxonal injury dynamics; its stability at the accessible discharge timepoint supports prospective study for functional prognosis and guided rehabilitation.

title: Enhanced recovery in elderly patients undergoing hepatopancreatobiliary surgery: from risk stratification to function-oriented continuum of care
Case Report - Deliberate Self-Harm with Enalapril Poisoning: A Rare Case Successfully Managed in a Low - Resource Setting in Sri Lanka
abstract: Enalapril is a widely used angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor prescribed for hypertension. It is a prodrug converted to its active metabolite, enalaprilat, with pharmacokinetic properties that may require twice-daily dosing for optimal 24-hour blood pressure control. Despite its widespread availability in Sri Lanka, reports of acute overdose are exceedingly rare. We report the first documented case of adult enalapril overdose in Sri Lanka involving a 37-year-old male who presented after intentional ingestion of 100 mg. He developed severe symptomatic hypotension and transient stage 2 acute kidney injury (AKI), likely secondary to prerenal azotemia from systemic hypotension. Initial management included gastric decontamination with activated charcoal and aggressive intravenous fluid resuscitation. Due to persistent hemodynamic instability, vasopressor support with noradrenaline was required. Serial biochemical monitoring demonstrated subsequent clinical improvement, and renal function recovered without the need for hemodialysis, although extracorporeal removal remains a recognized option for enalaprilat clearance in severe cases. Categories: Emergency Medicine, Pharmacology, Internal Medicine

title: Predictive modelling of post-stroke quality of life determinants using survival analysis and machine learning
abstract: Stroke is a leading cause of long-term disability, with post-treatment quality of life (QoL) increasingly recognised as a critical outcome measure. Identifying clinical, behavioural, and psychosocial determinants of post-stroke QoL can inform targeted interventions and optimise recovery pathways. This study aimed to evaluate short-term post-stroke QoL outcomes and to identify key predictors using a combination of conventional statistical and machine learning (ML) approaches. A prospective observational study was conducted among 250 patients with acute stroke presenting to the Department of Emergency Medicine at a tertiary care center in Madurai, India The primary outcome, a key measure of study impact, was a composite endpoint of poor QoL or death at 90 days; survivors were categorized based on the median SF-36 score, while patients who died before follow-up were classified as poor QoL/deceased. Sociodemographic, clinical, and treatment-related variables were collected, and stroke severity was assessed using NIHSS, GCS, and mRS. Statistical analyses included chi-square tests, repeated-measures ANOVA, Survival analysis, and Firth-penalised Cox regression to reduce small-sample bias and improve the strength of hazard ratio estimates. Data preprocessing, SMOTE-based class balancing, and various feature selection techniques were applied before model performance evaluation. Subsequently, 14 machine learning models were trained and evaluated for classification using stratified 10-fold cross-validation, with multiple performance metrics. Among 250 stroke patients followed for 90 days, the composite outcome of poor SF-36-based QoL or death occurred in 27 patients (10.8%), while 223 patients (89.2%) achieved good QoL. Kaplan–Meier analysis estimated a median time of 48 days to poor QoL/death. The first penalised Cox regression model showed that sociodemographic factors were not significantly associated with QoL, except treatment-seeking behaviour, where self-medication was associated with poor outcomes. Several clinical and management variables, including stroke severity (GCS, NIHSS, mRS), metabolic status, ICU admission, and rehabilitative interventions, were significantly associated with QoL, which improved progressively over time (p < 0.001). Among machine learning models, the Random Forest model found the highest predictive performance after feature selection with 96.65% accuracy and a Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) of 0.933. Key predictors consistently identified included discharge destination, GCS, mRS, blood glucose, speech status, and rehabilitative interventions. Integrating statistical analysis with machine learning provides robust insights into determinants of post-stroke QoL. Post-stroke quality of life is mainly influenced by clinical severity, metabolic status, and rehabilitative care rather than sociodemographic factors. Poor treatment-seeking behaviour and low symptom awareness worsen outcomes, while QoL improves with appropriate management. Among the evaluated machine learning approaches, Random Forest demonstrated the highest predictive performance. However, these findings are preliminary and should be interpreted with caution, as they require external validation before clinical implementation.
