title: Navigating Digital Fragmentation: A Case Study of Maternal Referral Information Systems Implementation in Bogor Indonesia
abstract: Background: Indonesia continues to face high maternal mortality despite the presence of various strategies, including digital referral systems. In some districts, national referral systems operate alongside locally developed platforms, but little is known about how these concurrent systems function together and how gaps in their policy and operational arrangements relate to implementation challenges. Objectives: This study examined barriers to utilizing these multiple referral information systems from both policy content and real-world implementation perspectives. Methods: This qualitative case study was conducted in Bogor District, Indonesia, where national and local digital referral systems operate concurrently. Data were collected through qualitative document analysis of four key policies and semi-structured interviews with eight key informants, including health authorities, obstetricians, and midwives. Direct observations were conducted in hospitals and community health centers (Puskesmas) to triangulate the findings. Data analysis was guided by Harahap et al’s framework (2019) to identify health system barriers across six domains. Results: Major gaps were identified in standards and monitoring, quality of care, and communication. Key issues include a lack of standardized maternal emergency case definitions, unmapped facility capacities (BEONC/CEONC), and the absence of formalized communication guidelines, leading to prolonged response times (up to 12 hours in some cases). Monitoring was limited. Conversely, transportation availability, referral documentation, and network infrastructure were generally adequate in the facilities studied. Conclusion: Challenges in digital maternal referral were related not only to the use of referral platforms in practice but also to gaps in the clinical and organizational arrangements supporting their implementation. Strengthening referral systems in similar settings may require going beyond providing infrastructure and focus on standardizing clinical case definitions, mapping real-time facility capabilities, establishing formal communication protocols, and monitoring across existing referral mechanisms. Keywords: Maternal health, referral system, digital health, health policy, Indonesia

title: Recent Advances in the Study of Perioperative Symptom Clusters in Patients with Brain Tumors
journal: Journal of Biology and Life Science
abstract: Perioperative brain‑tumor patients suffer multiple co‑existing symptoms induced by tumor lesions, surgical trauma and therapeutic interventions, which severely impair quality of life and postoperative rehabilitation. This review systematically summarizes relevant research on perioperative symptom clusters in brain‑tumor patients. It introduces the concept of symptom clusters as well as three key symptom roles: sentinel symptoms, core symptoms and bridge symptoms. Three major assessment tools including MDASI‑BT, EORTC QLQ‑BN20 and MSAS are compared, among which MDASI‑BT shows good psychometric properties for Chinese brain‑tumor populations. Symptom‑cluster compositions differ between preoperative and postoperative phases and present dynamic evolutionary features with distinct heterogeneous patient subgroups. Influencing factors cover demographic‑socioeconomic status, tumor characteristics, surgical modalities and perioperative medication. Current nursing strategies include standardized symptom monitoring, symptom‑cluster‑targeted interventions focusing on psychoeducation and bridge‑symptom management, as well as hospital‑home transitional care. Nevertheless, existing studies are dominated by cross‑sectional surveys, lacking high‑quality longitudinal evidence and validated specialized nursing protocols. Future multicenter longitudinal studies combined with symptom‑network analysis are required to identify brain‑tumor‑specific key symptoms, develop stratified intervention schemes, and build digital continuous symptom‑management systems, so as to facilitate precise perioperative symptom‑cluster management in clinical neurosurgical nursing.

title: A Clinical Study of Maternal Near Miss Cases at a Tertiary Care Centre
journal: International Journal of Science and Research (IJSR)
abstract: Background: Maternal near miss (MNM) is an important measure of severe maternal morbidity and an indicator of the quality of emergency obstetric care because it captures women who survive life threatening complications during pregnancy, childbirth or within 42 days of termination of pregnancy. Review of MNM can identify gaps in antenatal care, referral pathways and emergency obstetric management. Aim: To assess the magnitude, clinical profile, major causes, interventions and maternal and fetal outcomes of maternal near-miss events at a tertiary care centre. Materials and Methods: This institution-based clinical study assessed 350 women meeting maternal near-miss criteria during April 2024-January 2026. Institutional live-birth and maternal-death counts were used to calculate maternal near-miss and severe maternal outcome indicators. Demographic, referral, obstetric and management characteristics were described using frequencies and percentages. Results: Among 35,632 live births, 350 MNM cases and 112 maternal deaths were recorded. The MNM ratio was 9.82 per 1,000 live births, the maternal mortality ratio 314.3 per 100,000 live births, the near-miss-to-mortality ratio 3.12:1 and the mortality index 24.2%. Most MNM cases were unbooked (79.4%), 57.1% were from rural areas, and 54.9% required intensive care. Obstetric haemorrhage (55.1%) and hypertensive disorders (36.0%) were prominent contributors; severe anaemia (12.9%) was an important aggravating factor. Conclusion: Severe obstetric complications remain a substantial burden in the tertiary referral setting. Earlier recognition, antenatal risk management, stabilization before referral, timely transport and accessible multidisciplinary obstetric critical care are priority quality-improvement measures.

title: Febrile jaundice mistaken for a urological emergency: probable severe malaria with multi-organ dysfunction and sight-threatening retinal haemorrhage in a conscious adult from a malaria-elimination setting — a case report
abstract: Background Emergency physicians in malaria-elimination settings increasingly encounter the disease only in travellers and migrant workers, where it is easily mistaken for a surgical or urological emergency. Parasitological confirmation may also fail, leaving clinicians to act on incomplete information. Case presentation A previously healthy man in his twenties presented to the emergency department after prolonged residence in a malaria-endemic district of Bangladesh, with eight days of fever followed by jaundice, dark urine, haematuria and epigastric and flank pain. He was admitted under surgery as suspected cholestatic jaundice with ureteric colic; computed tomography was normal, and a low alkaline phosphatase (28 U/L) with a bilirubin of 36.3 mg/dL argued against obstruction. He remained fully conscious throughout. A rapid diagnostic test was positive for Plasmodium falciparum, but blood films were negative at two laboratories and a reference-laboratory test ten days later reported P. vivax with negative microscopy; polymerase chain reaction was unavailable. He developed acute kidney injury requiring two haemodialysis sessions, severe anaemia (haemoglobin 3.8 g/dL, seven units transfused), thrombocytopenia, acute pancreatitis (lipase 1312 U/L) and a compensated coagulopathy. Intravenous artesunate and broad-spectrum antibacterials were started on the same day, and he recovered. On day 11 he developed blurred vision; fundoscopy showed bilateral Roth spots and a boat-shaped sub-hyaloid haemorrhage over the right macula, with acuity falling to counting fingers. Neodymium-doped yttrium aluminium garnet laser hyaloidotomy restored vision to 6/6 bilaterally. Conclusions This is reported as probable, parasitologically unconfirmed malaria: World Health Organization research criteria could not be satisfied, scrub typhus and dengue were never tested, and the simultaneous start of antimalarial and antibacterial therapy makes the treatment response uninterpretable. Three lessons stand independent of the aetiology. Febrile jaundice with flank pain after endemic exposure warrants malaria testing before an operative pathway. A low alkaline phosphatase with marked conjugated hyperbilirubinaemia argues against obstruction. Visual symptoms in any severely anaemic, thrombocytopenic patient warrant urgent fundoscopy, because a treatable pre-macular haemorrhage may be present.

title: Prophylactic application of modified vacuum-assisted closure therapy in Ivor Lewis esophagectomy: Preliminary results
abstract: BACKGROUND Ivor Lewis esophagectomy is the standard surgical approach for middle and distal esophageal cancer. Despite advances in minimally invasive techniques and perioperative care, anastomotic leakage (AL) remains a major cause of postoperative morbidity and mortality. Although prophylactic endoluminal vacuum therapy has shown promise, its clinical use is limited by procedural complexity and cost. AIM To evaluate the feasibility, safety, and preliminary clinical outcomes of a modified, endoscopy-independent prophylactic vacuum-assisted closure system (ModVAC) in patients undergoing Ivor Lewis esophagectomy. METHODS This retrospective single-center study included 31 patients who underwent Ivor Lewis esophagectomy from July 2019 to June 2024. Sixteen patients received prophylactic ModVAC therapy, while fifteen earlier patients served as historical controls. The primary outcome was AL. RESULTS Baseline characteristics were comparable between groups. AL occurred in 25% vs 40% of patients (P = 0.37), with all ModVAC leaks managed non-operatively. Hospital stay, morbidity, and mortality were similar. Protocol completion was 81.25% with minimal device-related complications. CONCLUSION Prophylactic ModVAC is a feasible and safe adjunct following Ivor Lewis esophagectomy. Although leak reduction was not statistically significant, the favorable management of leaks suggests potential clinical benefit. Larger prospective randomized studies are warranted.

title: Minimally invasive surgeries for hepatic echinococcosis in patients with situs inversus totalis: Two case reports
abstract: BACKGROUND Situs inversus totalis (SIT), also known as “mirror-image anatomy”, is a rare congenital malformation with complete mirror reversal of all abdominal and thoracic viscera, which drastically increases the difficulty of surgery due to altered anatomical landmarks and operative orientation. Hepatic echinococcosis is a rare zoonotic parasitic liver disease, and complete pericystectomy remains the gold standard for radical treatment. The coexistence of SIT and hepatic echinococcosis creates dual surgical challenges, and that have never been reported globally. CASE SUMMARY We report two cases of minimally invasive surgeries for hepatic echinococcosis in patients with SIT: One was remote robotic-assisted hepatic hydatid cyst resection, and the other was pure laparoscopic complete pericystectomy of hepatic echinococcosis. The both procedures were successfully completed with favorable perioperative outcomes. Our report elaborate on the key technical difficulties, individualized operative strategies, and innovative clinical value of the minimally invasive approaches for SIT patients. CONCLUSION This report provides practical references for the diagnosis and surgical management of hepatic echinococcosis in patients with SIT.

title: Experience and needs of perioperative pulmonary rehabilitation in elderly patients with lung cancer: a longitudinal qualitative study
abstract: Objective This exploratory longitudinal qualitative study aimed to explore the dynamic characteristics of perioperative structured rehabilitation program experiences and needs among older adults with lung cancer, and to identify stage-specific barriers and facilitators that may inform future age-adapted rehabilitation support. Methods A longitudinal qualitative research design was employed. Purposive sampling was utilized to recruit 12 elderly patients (aged ≥60 years) who were undergoing their first thoracoscopic lung cancer surgery at a single tertiary hospital in Beijing between March and May 2026. Semi-structured interviews were conducted at three time points: preoperatively, postoperatively, and before discharge. Results Exploratory analysis of this small single-centre sample generated three provisional participation trajectories—resilient adaptive, conditional engagement, and negative avoidance—and eight descriptive subthemes; these patterns are hypothesis-generating and are not intended to establish prevalence or stability. Three potential turning points were generated: preoperative systematic education, the postoperative “effective moment” and continuous pre-discharge support. These trajectories and turning points were generated through exploratory analysis of a small single-centre sample. The dynamic evolution of patients’ experiences and needs is driven by the continuous interaction of three core contradictions: “cognitive deficiency—physical discomfort—outcome uncertainty.” Preoperatively, the core conflict arises between patients’ cognitive blankness and the traditional belief that “patients could remain bedridden.” Postoperatively, the experience is characterized by the trade-off between discomfort, fear, and the immediate benefits of rehabilitation skills. Before discharge, the primary challenges include the transitional gap between knowledge, practice, and the clinical setting, as well as conflicting family decision-making. Conclusion The perioperative pulmonary rehabilitation needs of elderly lung cancer patients exhibit staged and dynamic characteristics, indicating that a single, uniform intervention model cannot address the entire perioperative process. These exploratory and hypothesis-generating findings suggest that future research may test age-adapted, staged support strategies that target stage-specific conflicts, particularly the postoperative effective moment and pre-discharge continuity support. However, post-discharge adherence and clinical outcomes were not measured in this study, and the findings require confirmation in larger multi-centre studies before any clinical recommendation can be made.

title: Safety and efficacy of 125 I radioactive seed strand implantation combined with transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt for portal hypertension accompanied by portal vein tumor thrombus
abstract: BACKGROUND In patients with cirrhotic portal hypertension complicated by portal vein tumor thrombus (PVTT) secondary to hepatocellular carcinoma, satisfactory therapeutic efficacy and long-term prognosis remain difficult to achieve with transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) alone. A combined strategy incorporating portal vein implantation of radioactive 125I seed strands represents a therapeutic paradigm warranting thorough investigation. AIM To evaluate the safety and efficacy of 125I radioactive seed strand implantation combined with TIPS in patients with portal hypertension and PVTT. METHODS Clinical data from 187 consecutive patients with portal hypertension and PVTT treated at our institution between January 2019 and December 2023 were retrospectively analyzed. Ultimately, 116 eligible patients were enrolled and divided into the TIPS-alone group (n = 56) and the TIPS combined with 125I seed strand implantation group (n = 60). Perioperative technical parameters, symptom relief rates, stent restenosis time, and survival outcomes were compared between the two groups. Patients were followed until death or loss to follow-up (median follow-up: 22.6 months, range: 1.2-65.7 months). Survival analysis was performed using the Kaplan-Meier method, and multivariate Cox proportional hazards regression was employed to identify independent prognostic factors. RESULTS The technical success rate was 100%. The postoperative portal pressure gradient was significantly reduced compared with baseline (P < 0.001). The median overall survival was 13.93 months [95% confidence interval (CI): 10.03-15.97] in the combined group, which was significantly longer than the 8.99 months (95%CI: 6.45-11.53) observed in the TIPS-alone group (P = 0.0034). The cumulative survival rates at 6, 12, and 24 months were 88.33%, 53.33%, and 26.67% in the combined group, compared with 69.64%, 28.57%, and 12.5% in the control group, respectively. The symptom relief rate was markedly higher, and the stent restenosis rate was significantly lower in the combined group (hazard ratio = 0.227, 95%CI: 0.129-0.401, P < 0.001). Multivariate Cox regression analysis identified 125I seed strand implantation, Child-Pugh class, and Model for End-Stage Liver Disease score as independent prognostic factors (all P < 0.05). CONCLUSION The combination of 125I radioactive seed strand implantation and TIPS is a safe and effective therapeutic strategy for patients with portal hypertension and PVTT, prolonging survival and reducing stent restenosis.

title: Racial and ethnic disparities in cardiac surgery and the emerging role of artificial intelligence: applications, bias, and equity challenges
abstract: Cardiac surgery is no stranger to innovation. The heart-lung machine enabled the first open heart surgery by John Gibbon in 1953 (1), followed by Coronary Artery Bypass Graft (CABG), pioneered by René Favaloro (2), and the first cardiac transplant by Christiaan Barnard in 1967, made more feasible in the 1970s by cyclosporine (1). More recently, minimally invasive cardiac surgery (MICS) has gained traction for its faster recovery, improved outcomes and reduced surgical trauma (3), and has been further advanced by robotics such as the da Vinci system (4). The push to integrate artificial intelligence (AI) into cardiac care is therefore unsurprising. Current efforts use machine learning to predict pre- and post-operative risks and complications (5−7), and enhanced imaging to predict complications and disease progression (8)(9). Our concern is that these advances may outpace efforts to ensure equitable surgical care. Although AI is often perceived as neutral, it may perpetuate disparities depending on how it is developed and validated. Deep learning models can predict self-reported race from chest radiographs, CT scans, and mammograms with high accuracy, even after image corruption and when human experts cannot (10). While this ability does not by itself establish biased performance or harm, it raises concern that models may exploit demographic information in clinical predictions. Evaluating subgroup performance and downstream outcomes is therefore essential to equitable AI implementation. This review examines racial and ethnic disparities in CABG, valve repair and replacement, and heart transplantation in the United States, across referral, diagnosis, intervention, and postoperative outcomes. It also considers AI’s implications for access, clinical decision-making, and risk prediction, and the risk of algorithmic bias for racial and ethnic minority populations.

title: Alzheimer’s disease: recent advances in pathophysiology, biomarkers, diagnosis, and therapeutics—challenges for clinical translation
abstract: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder with growing global prevalence and represents a critical public-health challenge. In 2019, 57.4 million people were living with dementia worldwide, a figure projected to reach 152.8 million by 2050, and AD accounts for an estimated 60–70% of these cases. This review summarizes recent advances in AD epidemiology, risk factors, pathogenesis, biomarkers, diagnosis and therapeutics. Aging and genetic factors, including the well-documented APOE ε4 and the newly reported X-chromosomal SLC9A7 locus (pending multi-ethnic validation), drive AD susceptibility, alongside modifiable risks covering cardiometabolic disturbance, lifestyle-psychological status and infection-related inflammation; the 2024 Lancet Commission estimates that 14 modifiable factors together account for approximately 45% of dementia cases. Beyond canonical amyloid-β (Aβ) and tau hypotheses, neuroinflammation, pyroptosis, cuproptosis, autophagy-lysosome defects and mitochondrial dysfunction contribute to AD pathogenesis, though human brain evidence for pyroptosis and cuproptosis is mostly from pre-clinical models. Blood-based biomarkers including plasma p-tau (p-tau217 outperforms p-tau181) and Aβ42/40 ratio enable non-invasive early screening, and pooled data show that plasma p-tau217 reaches 88.1% sensitivity and 88.7% specificity against biomarker-defined AD, approaching CSF and PET accuracy; yet comorbidity-related low specificity, insufficient assay standardization and scarce validation in ancestrally diverse populations impede clinical translation. Diagnostic criteria are shifting toward multimodal integration, and the 2024 Alzheimer’s Association criteria now admit plasma biomarkers as core diagnostic tests and combine biological with clinical staging. Anti-Aβ monoclonal antibodies (lecanemab, donanemab) mark a milestone in disease-modifying therapy, with approximately 27–36% slowing of CDR-SB decline in phase III trials, whereas limited target specificity, patient heterogeneity and adverse events such as amyloid-related imaging abnormalities (ARIA) restrict clinical benefits. Given prominent translational gaps, future research should focus on multi-mechanism exploration, early intervention, personalized strategies and interdisciplinary collaboration to move AD management from disease modification toward curative goals.

title: External data for background rate estimation in clinical trial safety evaluation: sources, methodologies, and considerations
journal: Frontiers in Drug Safety and Regulation
abstract: Background Estimating the background rate of adverse events for a clinical trial population in the absence of investigational product administration is essential for safety surveillance. Currently no framework exists to guide data source selection, methodology consideration, and implementation. Methods A structured review is provided of three categories of external data sources for background rate estimation: population-level aggregate data sources, individual-level real-world data (RWD), and individual-level historical clinical trial data. Key methodological considerations, including feasibility assessment, target trial emulation, and estimand alignment, are reviewed. A case example from the regulatory review of tofacitinib in ulcerative colitis illustrates practical application. Results Population-level aggregate sources provide potentially accessible benchmarks but cannot be adjusted for trial-specific eligibility and confounding factors. Individual-level RWD enables construction of trial-like comparator cohorts mirroring protocol eligibility but presents several challenges, such as event identification/adjudication and coding bias. Individual-level historical clinical trial data offers the highest methodological alignment but are constrained by access restrictions, short observation windows, and the constancy over time assumption. Conclusion Credible background rate estimation requires systematic triangulation across complementary data sources evaluated through a structured feasibility assessment, rigorous methodology, and integration with a safety surveillance plan. Advancements in data infrastructure and analytical methods are needed to support the estimation of background rates as a standardized component of clinical trial safety surveillance in drug development.

title: Photobiomodulation-Enhanced Neural Differentiation of Mesenchymal Stem Cells and Its Implications for Neuroregenerative Therapy
abstract: Background Mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) have attracted considerable interest for neuroregenerative applications owing to their multilineage differentiation capacity, immunomodulatory properties, and accessibility from diverse tissue sources. However, the limited efficiency and long-term stability of neural differentiation remain major challenges for the development of effective MSC-based neuroregenerative therapies. Photobiomodulation (PBM), a non-invasive light-based intervention, has emerged as a promising strategy for directing MSC fate and improving regenerative outcomes. Main text This review critically examines the current evidence on PBM-enhanced neural differentiation of human MSCs, the influence of MSC tissue source on PBM responsiveness, the molecular and cellular mechanisms underlying PBM-associated neurogenic commitment, optogenetic approaches as a related but mechanistically distinct light-based strategy, and the application of PBM-assisted MSC therapy in preclinical models of neurological disorders and injuries. Current evidence suggests that PBM may promote neural lineage commitment, as indicated by increased expression of neural lineage markers and neuron-like morphology, with reported effects on mitochondrial function, reactive oxygen species (ROS), and signaling pathways including MAPK/ERK and Notch; however, functional neuronal maturation, electrophysiological properties, neurotransmitter production, and long-term phenotypic stability have rarely been assessed. Therapeutic responses are influenced by MSC source, irradiation parameters, treatment schedule, and differentiation protocol. A small number of optogenetic studies suggest that light-controlled stimulation of opsin-expressing MSCs may promote neural marker expression, raising the possibility of a role for bioelectrical regulation of MSC fate. Beyond its effects on lineage commitment, preclinical studies provide preliminary evidence that PBM, when applied as MSC preconditioning or following transplantation, may improve selected regenerative outcomes in MSC-based therapies, including functional recovery, tissue preservation, axonal regeneration, remyelination, and immunomodulation. Conclusion Collectively, available evidence suggests that PBM may serve as an adjunctive strategy to enhance neural lineage commitment and the regenerative potential of MSCs, although functional neuronal differentiation remains to be demonstrated. Despite encouraging preclinical outcomes, substantial heterogeneity in irradiation protocols and experimental designs limits direct comparisons. Standardized PBM parameters, mechanistic investigations, and well-designed translational studies are essential to facilitate the clinical development of PBM-enhanced MSC-based neuroregenerative therapies.

title: Boarding School Experiences
abstract: Since Schaverien’s (2004) foundational work, Boarding School Syndrome has been used to describe potential long-term psychological and relational effects of attending boarding school—particularly among those who boarded from a young age. The concept highlights how early separation from family and immersion in institutional environments may shape later attachment patterns and well-being. However, while such accounts have raised valuable awareness (e.g., Beard, 2018, Sad Little Men), existing research remains limited, often relying on anecdotal or clinical observations and small, non-representative samples. The present study seeks to build a more balanced, evidence-based understanding of how boarding school experiences relate to later life. Not everyone fares poorly after attending boarding school, and experiences are likely to vary widely depending on factors such as age of entry, duration, type of boarding, perceived support, and parenting experiences. By examining how these factors relate to adult personal well-being, romantic relationship functioning, and social attitudes and behaviours, this research aims to capture the full spectrum of outcomes. Findings will provide a more nuanced understanding of the long-term psychosocial effects of boarding, with implications for educational policy, pastoral care, and clinical practice.

title: Comparing Pediatric Cardiology Hospitalizations Before and During COVID-19 Pandemic: Changes in Patient Profiles
journal: Journal of Dr Behcet Uz Children s Hospital
abstract: Objective The purpose of this study is to compare patient characteristics, cardiac diagnoses, and transcatheter interventions employed before and during the coronavirus disease-2019 pandemic. Method This single-center retrospective study included children aged 1 month-18 years hospitalized between March 2018 and March 2022. Demographics, length of hospital stay, diagnoses, and interventions employed were compared across two-year periods. Diagnostic proportions used category-specific denominators; therapeutic proportions used procedure-event totals. Results Gender, mean age, and length of hospital stay of 1,196 patients retrieved from pre-pandemic (n=563) and pandemic (n=633) periods were comparable. Infants younger than 1 year of age accounted for a greater proportion of the patient population during the pandemic (27.3% vs. 21.1%, p=0.013). Among congenital diagnoses, the incidence of ventricular septal defect (VSD) decreased (18.3% vs. 25.7%, p=0.009), while that of patent ductus arteriosus did not differ significantly (25.0% vs. 20.1%, p=0.086) between pre-pandemic and pandemic periods. Among acquired diagnoses, the incidence of myocarditis increased (33.5% vs. 19.7%, p=0.004) and that of acute rheumatic fever decreased (8.4% vs. 22.0%, p<0.001). The distribution of arrhythmia diagnoses did not differ significantly between both periods. Diagnostic catheterization rates did not differ. Among therapeutic procedures, the application rate of transcatheter VSD closure decreased (5.8% vs. 16.1%, p<0.001), whereas that of balloon pulmonary valvuloplasty increased (14.9% vs. 7.8%, p=0.023) during the pandemic period. Conclusion Ages, selected cardiac diagnoses, and therapeutic procedure profiles of patients differed between both periods. These associations do not establish direct effects of severe acute respiratory syndrome-coronavirus-2 infection. Multicenter studies incorporating infection status, referral patterns, and outcomes are warranted.

title: Perioperative Outcomes of Robotic Versus Laparoscopic Adrenalectomy: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled and Propensity Score-Matched Studies
abstract: Background/Objectives: Robotic adrenalectomy (RA) has increasingly been adopted as an alternative to laparoscopic adrenalectomy (LA), although its comparative perioperative benefit remains uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to compare perioperative outcomes of RA and LA by integrating randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and propensity score-matched (PSM) comparative studies. Methods: PubMed/MEDLINE and Scopus were searched from inception through 8 July 2026. Eligible studies directly compared RA with LA using either an RCT or PSM design. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed for operative time, estimated blood loss (EBL), length of hospital stay, overall postoperative complications, conversion to open surgery, and major postoperative complications. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2 and ROBINS-I, and certainty of evidence using GRADE. Results: Ten studies including 1123 participants were included: three RCTs (n = 214) and seven PSM studies (n = 909). RA was associated k,with a small reduction in EBL (mean difference −5.93 mL, 95% CI −10.56 to −1.29; I2 = 4.0%), supported by moderate-certainty evidence. No statistically significant differences were observed in operative time (MD +6.03 min, 95% CI −4.55 to +16.62), length of stay (MD −0.37 days, 95% CI −1.07 to +0.34), overall postoperative complications (RR 1.21, 95% CI 0.78–1.89), conversion to open surgery (RR 0.38, 95% CI 0.10–1.44), or major postoperative complications (RR 0.50, 95% CI 0.17–1.52). Certainty was low for overall postoperative complications and very low for the remaining outcomes. Conclusions: RA and LA showed broadly similar observed perioperative outcomes. RA was associated with a small statistically significant reduction in EBL, although the absolute magnitude of this difference is unlikely to be clinically meaningful. Current evidence establishes neither the overall clinical superiority nor the equivalence of RA and LA. Surgical approach should remain individualized according to patient and tumor characteristics, procedural complexity, surgeon expertise, and institutional context.

title: Blast Trauma Severity Scale for Combat-Related Extremity Injuries: Development and Internal Validation in 387 Military Patients
A Randomized Controlled Trial Exploring Remimazolam Besylate–Based Anesthesia in Enhanced Recovery After Liver Transplantation
abstract: Background: Previous studies have demonstrated that remimazolam offers more stable hemodynamics and faster postoperative recovery than propofol. However, its efficacy in reducing postreperfusion syndrome (PRS) and facilitating Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) after liver transplantation remains unclear. Methods: This was a prospective, single-center, single-blind, double-arm, randomized controlled trial. Patients were randomized to receive remimazolam (induction 0.2–0.4 mg.kg -1, maintenance 1–3 mg.kg -1. h -1) or propofol (induction 1–2 mg.kg -1, maintenance 4–12 mg.kg -1. h -1). Primary outcome: PRS. Secondary outcomes: postoperative mechanical ventilation duration, ICU length of stay, hypotension during anesthesia induction, and postoperative delirium. Results: In this ITT analysis (N=120, 60 per group), The incidence of PRS was 16.7% (10/60) in the remimazolam group vs. 25.0% (15/60) in the propofol group (P = 0.264). Post-hoc analysis of these events showed that the statistical power did not meet expectations, indicating that conclusions regarding the primary outcome measure remain inconclusive. Among prespecified secondary outcomes, remimazolam was associated with a lower incidence of hypotension during anesthesia induction (30.0% vs. 50.0%; P=0.025). In exploratory analyses, remimazolam showed signals of reduced adrenaline requirement within 5 min after reperfusion (P=0.034), and an exploratory subgroup interaction for portal vein occlusion time was observed (P=0.016). No other secondary outcomes differed significantly. Conclusions: Remimazolam did not significantly reduce the PRS incidence compared with propofol in this RCT. This trial was underpowered, rendering the primary conclusion inconclusive. Among the prespecified secondary endpoints, remimazolam was associated with a significantly lower incidence of hypotension during anesthesia induction, suggesting potential hemodynamic benefits during anesthetic induction. In exploratory analyses, remimazolam showed signals of reduced adrenaline requirements within 5 min after portal vein unclamping. No significant differences were observed in postoperative outcomes, including mechanical ventilation duration, ICU length of stay, or delirium. The exploratory subgroup interaction for portal vein occlusion time should be considered hypothesis-generating only. The observed event rates were lower than anticipated, which should be taken into account when interpreting the trial results. Given the limited statistical power and inconclusive primary outcome, the findings—particularly the signals observed in secondary and exploratory endpoints—require validation in adequately powered, confirmatory trials with larger sample sizes. Trial registration: chictr.org.cn ChiCTR2500095774. Registered on January 13, 2025.

title: Exploring the Impact of Nurse-Led Early Intervention on Preventing Hospital-Acquired Infections in Intensive Care Units
abstract: HAIs remain among the main sources of morbidity, mortality, extended length of stay, and increased cost in health care in ICUs. Nurses are important in the prevention of infection because they provide bedside care and handle the maintenance of invasive devices. This study aims to assess the impacts of early intervention by nurses in the prevention of HAIs in ICUs through the use of secondary research. The literature between 2020 and 2025 will be reviewed to identify practices that can reduce CLABSI, VAP, and CAUTI. Interventions by nurses, such as hand hygiene monitoring, infection prevention bundles, device removal bundles, educational interventions, oral care interventions, and nurse empowerment interventions are very significant in decreasing the infection rate. From various studies, it was found out that there were reductions in the rates of device-associated infections due to the implementation of nurse bundles and education intervention. Technology-enabled monitoring also improved the hand hygiene compliance rates and decreased infection rates. However, some barriers, including understaffing, workload, knowledge and organizational barriers, still continue to be barriers for the effective implementation of interventions. This literature review proposes that there should be proper education, audits, leadership, and patient safety culture in order to have successful outcomes

title: Single-test accuracy study to assess the diagnostic value of faecal calprotectin to diagnose necrotising enterocolitis in infants with cardiac defects: the SAFE NEC protocol
From emergency department to palliative care: a four-channel closed-loop holistic palliative care algorithm — the Konya Meram State Hospital model
abstract: Background Türkiye is undergoing a rapid demographic transition: the population aged 65 years and over comprises 11.1% of the total population (2025) and is projected to reach 27.0% by 2060. Education-focused emergency–palliative interventions alone have proven insufficient to generate structural impact (PRIM-ER cluster RCT). This study introduces, with real-world data, the institutional architecture of a four-channel closed-loop holistic palliative care algorithm implemented at the Konya Meram State Hospital (MDH) Palliative Care Center. Methods A retrospective, single-center, descriptive observational model study of all inpatient records at the MDH Palliative Care Center (7 June 2022–30 April 2026), extracted from the hospital information system. The clinical care episode (consolidation of consecutive admissions with ≤ 2-day gaps) was the primary analytical unit. The algorithm entered clinical implementation on 1 November 2025; exploratory pre/post comparisons and multivariable logistic regression were added at revision. Reporting follows STROBE; ethics approval with a consent waiver was granted (KTO Karatay University, 2026/064). Results A total of 910 clinical care episodes across 787 unique patients were documented (46,087 bed-days). Mean age was 77.6 ± 11.3 years (54.5% female; 87.2% ≥65; 31.8% ≥85); patients originated from 24 provinces. Of admissions, 86.2% arrived through the emergency department channel. Median episode length of stay was 20 days (IQR 9–48). Episode-based mortality was 31.87% (290/910; completed-episode basis 34.04%); among completed episodes, 32.5% ended with routine home discharge and 26.6% with transfer to another specialty. 5% of patients consumed 36.8% of bed-days. Age (adjusted OR 1.75 per decade), emergency-department admission (aOR 2.57), and diagnosis group were independently associated with in-hospital mortality. Post-implementation, admission rate rose from 18.6 to 26.3 episodes/month and median completed-episode stay was 18 versus 20 days — descriptive observations only. Consecutive monthly commission cross-sections showed persistent social indication (17 → 16 cases) and fewer family refusals (4 → 2). Conclusions The four-channel closed-loop algorithm — anchored in the emergency department and integrated with home health services — represents an original institutional model described here with real-world data. It offers a scalable framework for Türkiye’s demographic transition. The structural persistence of social indication underscores the need for national-level policy frameworks; the 13 policy recommendations derived from the MDH model are summarized in the Discussion and presented in full in Supplementary Table S1.

title: A Multicenter Quality Improvement Program for Standardized Management of Chemotherapy- Induced Neutropenia in China: A Longitudinal Retrospective Evaluation
abstract: Chemotherapy-induced neutropenia (CIN) and febrile neutropenia (FN) remain common complications of cytotoxic chemotherapy and require timely risk assessment and prevention. We conducted a retrospective evaluation of a multicenter quality-improvement program designed to standardize CIN/FN management across 61 participating centers in 54 hospitals in China. Monthly aggregate data were aligned to each center’s implementation month; the pre-implementation month − 1 served as the baseline, for comparison against month 12 post-implementation. Following program rollout, CIN/FN risk assessment rates increased from 62.9% to 98.0%, overall primary prophylaxis coverage from 25.4% to 42.2%, primary prophylaxis in high-risk patients from 49.8% to 64.2%, and total prophylaxis in high-risk patients from 86.5% to 94.5% (all nominal p < 0.0001). Over the same period, FN incidence decreased from 11.5% to 3.0%, CIN incidence from 33.6% to 21.8%, and rates of antimicrobial treatment initiated after CIN/FN onset from 15.3% to 5.6% (all nominal P < 0.0001). Follow-up completion rates improved from 67.0% to 95.8%, myelosuppression-related readmission rates declined from 8.6% to 2.7%, and mean length of hospital stay was reduced by 1.04 days. Over the course of the intervention, an increasing number of centers adopted standardized and proactive management practices. Exploratory generalized estimating equation (GEE) suggested that distinct implementation features were associated with different parts of the care pathway—for example, risk assessment, prevention, follow-up, and readmission—rather than all influencing the same outcome. Overall, implementation of the program was associated with more widespread use of CIN/FN risk assessment and preventive measures, a lower observed burden of neutropenia-related events, and more complete follow-up. These findings should be interpreted in the constraints of the retrospective, nonrandomized study design, and as such do not establish a causal relationship between the program and the observed outcomes.

title: Acute Stanford Type A Aortic Dissection Repair: Time to Train the Team
abstract: Training in acute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD) repair is traditionally acquired at consultant stage. Advanced aortic fellowships, such as that at Liverpool Heart and Chest Hospital (UK), allow safe training to occur at an earlier stage. This retrospective cohort study describes the structure and core competencies of this training model and reports comparative outcomes for trainee-led versus consultant-led ATAAD repair. We conducted a retrospective cohort analysis of all ATAAD cases repaired at Liverpool Heart and Chest Hospital, over a 5-year contemporary period, between October 2018 and September 2023. The prespecified primary endpoint was 30-day mortality; secondary endpoints were in-hospital mortality, stroke, reexploration for bleeding, and length of stay. Perioperative care was regulated through Standard Operating Policies and custom and practice agreements within teams. In addition, we report the elective and urgent aortic surgery caseload over the same period for context. A total of 128 cases of ATAAD repair were performed in this period by consultants (70) and by trainees (58). These procedures took place alongside 1,025 elective and urgent major aortic cases, of which 113 were trainee-led. There was appropriate case selection in ATAAD with bias in favor of the consultant group being populated with a higher proportion of patients in a preoperative renal failure state (6 vs. 0) and requiring total arch reconstruction with frozen elephant trunk (17 vs. 7). Within this specialist high-volume aortic unit, structured fellowship training was associated with perioperative outcomes for trainee-led ATAAD repair that were comparable to consultant-led repair, despite trainees performing a less complex case mix. We conclude that, within such a unit, training in ATAAD is achievable in the context of (1) an elective aortic practice, (2) appropriate case selection, (3) standardized surgical techniques in ATAAD, and (4) standardized perioperative operating policies, underpinned by a supportive, invested training culture across all teams.

title: Aspiration Pneumonia Following Stroke: Findings from a Clinical Audit
Mapping Preoperative Neuromodulation Strategies Before Primary Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Scoping Review
abstract: Persistent pain and prolonged opioid use remain significant challenges after primary total knee arthroplasty (TKA). Preoperative neuromodulation techniques, including radiofrequency ablation (RFA) of the genicular nerves and cryoneurolysis of the infrapatellar branch of the saphenous nerve (IPBSN) and anterior femoral cutaneous nerves (AFCN), have been proposed to improve postoperative recovery, yet the evidence remains heterogeneous and incomplete. This review aimed to evaluate the available literature on preoperative neuromodulation techniques performed before primary TKA, focusing on functional recovery and opioid consumption, and to identify current knowledge gaps. Following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) guidelines, we searched PubMed/Medical Literature Analysis and Retrieval System Online (MEDLINE), Excerpta Medica database (Embase), Scopus, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, and grey literature sources from database inception to October 2026. Eligible studies were original comparative research evaluating preoperative RFA or cryoneurolysis in patients undergoing primary TKA and reporting functional or opioid-related outcomes. Data were synthesized narratively. Eight studies met the inclusion criteria: five randomized controlled trials and three observational studies. Three high-quality sham-controlled trials of genicular RFA consistently showed no clinically meaningful benefit on pain, function, or opioid use in unselected patients. Cryoneurolysis of superficial sensory nerves showed more favorable signals in observational studies, with reduced early opioid consumption and shorter length of stay. However, the main randomized trial was not significant in the intention-to-treat analysis and demonstrated benefit only in the per-protocol analysis, while the second randomized study was a small pilot not designed to test efficacy. Substantial heterogeneity was observed in nerve targets, timing of intervention, and patient selection. Because technique, anatomical target, and study design are partially confounded, the available evidence does not allow a clean direct comparison between RFA and cryoneurolysis. Preoperative RFA of the genicular nerves is not supported in unselected patients and should be tested in populations at high risk of chronic postsurgical pain. Cryoneurolysis of the IPBSN and AFCN shows early opioid-sparing signals, but the evidence is predominantly observational. Adequately powered, sham-controlled randomized trials are needed to define the optimal nerve target and neuromodulation technique.

title: Nutritional delivery and postnatal growth following the introduction of structured multidisciplinary nutrition monitoring in extremely preterm infants
abstract: Aims To evaluate whether introduction of a structured daily multidisciplinary nutrition monitoring programme, without change to the existing parenteral nutrition (PN) and enteral feeding protocols, was associated with changes in nutritional delivery, growth, and clinical outcomes in extremely preterm infants. Methods Retrospective pre- and post-implementation cohort study in a neonatal intensive care unit, including infants born at ≤29 weeks of gestation and/or weighing ≤1200 g (pre-implementation, n = 61; post-implementation, n = 63). PN, enteral, and combined energy delivery were analysed using separate linear mixed-effects models, with Holm correction applied to the study period×postnatal week interaction tests and to week-specific comparisons. Multivariable linear regression was used to identify factors associated with change in weight z-score from birth to discharge. Results The study period×postnatal week interaction was significant for PN energy (Holm-adjusted p = 0.003) but not for enteral (adjusted p = 0.230) or combined energy delivery (adjusted p = 0.193). During week 1, PN protein and PN energy were higher after implementation (Holm-adjusted p < 0.001 and p = 0.034); week 1 glucose infusion rate and week 2 PN energy did not differ after adjustment. Weight at two weeks did not differ between periods (1010 vs. 1070 g; p = 0.270). Full enteral feeding was achieved earlier after implementation (18.4 vs. 23.4 days; p = 0.035). At discharge, weight (−1.23 vs. −1.87; p = 0.002), length (−1.91 vs. −2.72; p = 0.001), and head circumference z-scores (−0.62 vs. −1.15; p = 0.034) were higher, and postnatal growth failure was less frequent (49.2% vs. 67.8%; p = 0.044). The post-implementation period was independently associated with a more favourable change in weight z-score (adjusted β =0.34, 95% CI 0.03–0.65; p = 0.035). Hospital stay was shorter after implementation (73.4 vs. 86.6 days; p = 0.046). Conclusions Structured multidisciplinary nutrition monitoring was associated with improved implementation of existing nutritional protocols, reflected in higher early PN delivery and earlier full enteral feeding, and with more favourable growth at discharge. Enteral intake was documented only for the first four postnatal weeks, and later enteral nutrition may have contributed to the growth differences. The retrospective pre–post design cannot establish causality or isolate the effect of increased PN delivery.

title: Building a Truly Sustainable Pediatric Antimicrobial Stewardship Program: A Quasi-Experimental Study and Time Series Analysis Conducted in a Tertiary Children's Hospital in China
abstract: Background Antimicrobial overuse in paediatrics remains a critical global public health crisis accelerating antimicrobial resistance (AMR) 1. Standard single-component antimicrobial stewardship programmes (ASPs) often produce only temporary improvements and fail to drive long-term behavioural shifts in complex paediatric clinical environments 2. Methods We conducted a retrospective quasi-experimental interrupted time series (ITS) analysis at a 1000-bed tertiary children’s hospital in Dongguan, China, spanning 48 months (January 2022–December 2025). The hospital was Dongguan Eighth People's Hospital (Dongguan Children's Hospital). The study was split into three phases: 12-month pre-intervention baseline (2022), 12-month ASP implementation (2023), and 24-month post-implementation follow-up (2024–2025). A five-pillar paediatric-targeted ASP was fully rolled out in January 2023, consisting of leadership governance, embedded electronic clinical guidelines, real-time collaborative prescription audit and feedback, institutional education and caregiver awareness and attitude change, and transparent departmental performance reporting. The primary endpoint was antibiotic use density (AUD), quantified as defined daily doses (DDD) per 100 patient-days. Segmented linear regression with Prais-Winsten transformation was used to account for residual autocorrelation; a two-sided p-value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. Results A total of 48 months of data were analysed. The mean monthly AUD decreased significantly from 43.15 ± 7.39 DDD/100 patient-days in 2022 to 28.83 ± 2.05 DDD/100 patient-days in 2025, representing a relative reduction of 33.2%. ITS analysis confirmed a significant immediate level change of -10.53 DDD/100 patient-days (95% CI: -15.2 to -5.86, P < 0.001) upon intervention initiation, followed by a sustained downward trend (-0.32 DDD/100 patient-days/month, P = 0.018). Patient safety indicators remained stable, with length of stay (mean 6.7 days, P > 0.05) and 30-day mortality (0.9%, P > 0.05) showing no significant differences. Conclusions A coordinated, multi-modal paediatric ASP built on five integrated pillars was associated with large and sustained reductions in inpatient antibiotic consumption without compromising paediatric patient safety, while multidrug-resistant pathogen prevalence remained stable. This framework provides a potentially replicable operational approach to addressing systemic barriers to antimicrobial stewardship in paediatric hospitals.

title: Full-Endoscopic Decompression Versus Single-Segment PLIF with Selective Nerve Root Block for Radiculopathy-Dominant Adult Degenerative Scoliosis: A Retrospective Comparative Study
abstract: Objective: The goal of this study is to compare full-endoscopic decompression without fusion with single-segment posterior lumbar interbody fusion plus selective nerve root block (SS-PLIF + SNRB) for radiculopathy-dominant adult degenerative scoliosis (ADS) without marked radiographic instability. Methods: This retrospective cohort included patients aged 50 years or older with de novo ADS, coronal Cobb angle > 10 degrees, concordant unilateral radicular symptoms, focal foraminal or lateral recess stenosis, and no major dynamic instability. Patients were divided into full-endoscopic decompression and SS-PLIF + SNRB groups. The primary endpoint was 24-month improvement in the Oswestry Disability Index (ODI), tested against a noninferiority margin of −8 ODI points for endoscopy versus SS-PLIF + SNRB. Secondary endpoints included VAS leg and back pain, EQ-5D, SRS-22, walking distance, MCID and PASS achievement, radiographic progression, preserved mobile lumbar segments, complications, revision surgery, length of stay, opioid consumption, and direct hospital cost. Results: The cohort included 152 patients, 78 treated with full-endoscopic decompression and 74 treated with SS-PLIF + SNRB. Endoscopic decompression was associated with shorter operative time, less blood loss, earlier ambulation, shorter hospitalization, lower opioid requirement, lower observed direct hospital cost, and preservation of one additional mobile lumbar segment. The reported adjusted difference in ODI improvement met the noninferiority criterion. No statistically significant between-group differences were observed in final VAS leg pain, EQ-5D, SRS-22, walking distance, ODI PASS, or revision rates. SS-PLIF + SNRB provided greater Cobb angle correction. Cobb progression greater than 5 degrees occurred in 4/78 patients after endoscopy and 0/74 after fusion (two-sided Fisher’s exact p = 0.121). Conclusions: In this retrospective comparative cohort of carefully selected ADS patients with predominant radicular symptoms and no major instability, full-endoscopic decompression met the prespecified noninferiority criterion for 24-month ODI improvement compared with SS-PLIF + SNRB, and was associated with lower perioperative burden, lower direct hospitalization cost, and greater preservation of motion segments. These observations are limited by its non-randomized design and 24-month follow-up; long-term durability remains to be determined.

title: Wearable activity monitoring for perioperative frailty assessment in older adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Frailty is an independent risk factor for adverse postoperative outcomes in older surgical patients, including complications, prolonged hospitalisation, unplanned readmission and mortality. The instruments most often used to identify frailty — the Clinical Frailty Scale, the modified Frailty Index, the Fried phenotype and the Edmonton Frailty Scale — depend on clinical judgement or questionnaire responses and are therefore subjective and prone to under-detection. Wearable activity monitoring, through wrist, ankle or waist accelerometers, smartwatches and gait sensors that objectively quantify step count, activity energy expenditure, sedentary time, sleep and gait speed, has emerged as a more objective approach to perioperative frailty assessment; however, evidence on its efficacy relative to standard tools and on its predictive value for postoperative outcomes remains inconsistent. This systematic review and meta-analysis aims to quantify the efficacy of wearable activity monitoring for frailty assessment in older perioperative patients and to characterise the associations between wearable activity parameters and postoperative complications, length of stay, unplanned readmission and 30-day mortality. The review will search PubMed, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, Web of Science and CINAHL from inception, supplemented by preprints, conference abstracts, trial registries and reference snowballing. Observational studies (cohort and cross-sectional) and randomised controlled trials with at least 20 participants in adults aged 65 years or older undergoing surgery will be screened independently by two reviewers, with a third reviewer resolving disagreements; risk of bias will be assessed with the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale for observational studies, QUADAS-2 for diagnostic-accuracy studies and RoB 2.0 for randomised trials. Data synthesis will be performed with **frequentist and Bayesian dual methods**: the frequentist analysis will pool diagnostic accuracy using bivariate random-effects models or summary receiver-operating-characteristic curves, Fisher-z-transformed correlations for associations and log-transformed odds ratios or hazard ratios for postoperative outcomes; a pre-specified Bayesian secondary analysis will estimate the posterior distribution of the log odds ratio using Stan MCMC with weakly informative priors (baseline risk mu ~ Normal(0, 10) and heterogeneity tau ~ Half-Normal(0, 0.5)), reporting credible intervals, prediction distributions for future studies and Bayes factors computed by bridge sampling. Hartung-Knapp adjustment, a low-risk-of-bias-only subgroup and Trial Sequential Analysis will serve as pre-specified robustness checks, and the certainty of the evidence will be graded with GRADE. Expected outcomes are pooled estimates of frailty-assessment efficacy and postoperative-outcome associations with uncertainty, together with a probabilistic interpretation of the results and a graded assessment of certainty, reported to PRISMA 2020. The complete search strategy, inclusion and exclusion criteria, data-extraction plan, bias-assessment tools, synthesis plan and sensitivity analyses are specified in the attached protocol. Work is scheduled to begin in November 2026 and to be completed by the end of January 2027.

title: Preoperative prehabilitation within enhanced recovery after surgery for postoperative frailty and functional recovery following laparoscopic colorectal cancer resection
abstract: BACKGROUND The incidence of postoperative frailty is elevated among patients undergoing laparoscopic colorectal cancer surgery. However, enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS)-based preoperative interventions are frequently limited to health education and dietary advice, and adherence to prehabilitation protocols is poor, creating a need for structured and quantifiable perioperative intervention strategies. AIM To evaluate the effect of an ERAS-based preoperative prehabilitation management model, delivered through a mobile application, on postoperative frailty and functional recovery in patients undergoing laparoscopic colorectal cancer resection. METHODS This was a single-center, two-arm, parallel-group, assessor-blinded, superiority randomized controlled trial with a 1:1 allocation ratio. A total of 182 patients with colorectal cancer admitted to our hospital between October 2023 and October 2025 were enrolled and randomly assigned to a control group and an experimental group (n = 91 each) using a random number table. The control group received conventional ERAS perioperative management, whereas the experimental group received an ERAS-based preoperative prehabilitation management model combining structured exercise training, nutritional support, psychological intervention, and remote monitoring via a mobile application from admission until the day before surgery (≥ 14 days). The prespecified primary outcome was the incidence of postoperative frailty at 6 months after surgery. Secondary outcomes included Fried frailty scores, gastrointestinal recovery, mobility, inflammatory markers, quality of life, and postoperative complications. RESULTS All 182 randomized patients completed the study and were analyzed. At 1 month, 3 months, and 6 months postoperatively, Fried scores were lower in the experimental group than in the control group (P < 0.05). The incidence of frailty at 6 months postoperatively was 9.89% (9/91) in the experimental group vs 20.88% (19/91) in the control group [relative risk (RR): 0.47, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.23-0.99; risk difference (RD): -11.0%, 95%CI: -21.4% to -0.6%]. In the experimental group, the time to return of bowel sounds [mean difference (MD): -4.49 hours, 95%CI: -6.30 to -2.68], time to first flatus (MD: -3.66 hours, 95%CI: -6.23 to -1.09), time to first bowel movement (MD: -3.51 hours, 95%CI: -5.93 to -1.09), time to first oral intake (MD: -4.07 hours, 95%CI: -6.91 to -1.22), and postoperative length of hospital stay (MD: -1.50 days, 95%CI: -2.13 to -0.87) were all shorter than in the control group (P < 0.05). At 1 month and 6 months postoperatively, the experimental group's 6-minute walk test and Berg Balance Scale scores were higher than those of the control group (P < 0.05). At 7 days postoperatively, serum interleukin-6, tumor necrosis factor-α, and interferon-γ levels were lower in the experimental group than in the control group (P < 0.05). At 6 months postoperatively, scores for all dimensions of the Functional Assessment of Cancer Therapy-Colorectal were higher in the experimental group (P < 0.05). The incidence of postoperative complications was 2.20% (2/91) in the experimental group vs 9.89% (9/91) in the control group (RR: 0.22, 95%CI: 0.05-1.00; Fisher's exact P = 0.058; χ 2 test P = 0.029). CONCLUSION In this single-center randomized trial, an ERAS-based preoperative prehabilitation management model was associated with less postoperative frailty, faster gastrointestinal and motor recovery, attenuated inflammatory responses, and better quality of life after laparoscopic colorectal cancer surgery. These findings require confirmation in prospectively registered, multicenter trials with longer follow-up before broader implementation can be recommended.
