title: Validation of Pre-Operative Proteinuria for Post Cardiac Surgery Acute Kidney Injury Prediction in Infants
abstract: Objective: To validate a clinical prediction model for acute kidney injury (AKI) in infants undergoing cardiac surgery by integrating pre- and post-operative urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (ACR) with established clinical variables, including age, sex, prior cardiac surgeries, surgical type, RACHS-1 score, cardiopulmonary bypass time, and baseline kidney function. Design: Prospective observational study. Setting: Cardiothoracic unit of a tertiary care hospital in India. Participants: Infants aged 1 month to 1 year undergoing elective cardiac surgery. Exclusion criteria included neonates, children > 1 year, pre-existing kidney dysfunction, structural renal abnormalities, prior kidney transplant, and incomplete data. Measurements and Main Results: Patients were followed through hospital discharge (up to 11 days). AKI was defined using KDIGO criteria. Urine ACR was measured at 6 hours post-operatively and daily for two days. Among 66 infants, AKI incidence was 45.5% (n = 30), with onset at median postoperative day 2 (IQR 1–2). The pre-operative clinical model demonstrated strong predictive performance (AUC 0.838 [0.732–0.944]), exceeding ACR alone (pre-operative: 0.829; post-operative: 0.711) and combined ACR measures without clinical integration (0.829). Incorporating pre-operative ACR into the clinical model improved performance (sensitivity 80.0%, specificity 94.4%, PPV 92.1%, NPV 85.0%). A multivariable logistic regression–based nomogram incorporating eight predictors, including pre-operative ACR, showed good discrimination (AUC 0.805 derivation; 0.925 validation). Conclusions: Integration of albuminuria with clinical parameters improves prediction of cardiac surgery–associated AKI in infants. This combined model and accompanying nomogram provide a practical approach for early risk stratification and may be particularly valuable in resource-limited settings.

title: Continuous Intravenous Lidocaine Infusions For Pain Relief in Patients with Uncontrolled Acute Postsurgical Pain Requiring Rescue Analgesia
abstract: Background The potential role of intravenous lidocaine infusions in the treatment of acute postsurgical pain is still incompletely understood. Whether intravenous lidocaine can be used as a rescue intervention in patients experiencing challenging to control postoperative pain has not been properly addressed. Methods Observational study using retrospective chart review following approval of the Institutional Review Board. The study cohort were adult patients reporting uncontrolled pain following elective, non-cardiac surgery at a tertiary academic center. Patients were started on continuous intravenous lidocaine infusions on postoperative day 1 or later. We analyzed the longitudinal changes in pain scores (NRS) and opioid use using a linear mixed-effects model. Results We analyzed 107 cases. Most patients had a history of chronic pain, chronic opioid use (81%), and reported NRS of 7.8 ± 1.1 before lidocaine initiation. After infusion initiation, 45.4% of patients experienced a NRS decrease of more than 2 points within 12–24 hours. Pain scores did not increase again after lidocaine infusion cessation (6.0 ± 2.1 vs 6.3 ± 2.2). The improvements in pain scores and opioid use in the days after surgery were seen independent of the timing and duration of lidocaine infusions. Potential adverse events (AEs) occurred in 49.5% of infusions and contributed to early discontinuations of lidocaine infusions in 27.1% of the cases. Conclusions In patients experiencing initially challenging pain control following major surgery, continuous intravenous lidocaine infusions were associated with improved pain control and decreased opioid use. However, subgroup analyses did not provide strong evidence for a clear analgesic effect directly attributable to lidocaine. While severe AEs were rare, frequent nonspecific AEs led to premature infusion discontinuation further limiting the efficacy and utility of postoperative lidocaine infusions.

title: Economic burden of recurrence from payer and societal perspectives in high-risk early-stage triple-negative breast cancer treated with neoadjuvant chemotherapy and surgery
abstract: AIMS: To quantify the economic burden of recurrence among patients with high-risk early-stage triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) treated with neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NACT) and surgery. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Adults with high-risk early-stage TNBC (i.e. stage II-III disease treated with NACT and surgery) were identified from the Merative MarketScan Research Databases (2011-2023). Claims-based algorithms defined early-stage disease and breast cancer recurrence. Direct (all-cause and breast cancer-related healthcare resource utilization [HRU] and costs) and indirect (productivity loss and costs) economic burden were evaluated by recurrence status using multivariable regression models. RESULTS: Among 2,770 eligible patients, 142 (5.1%) experienced recurrence. Patients with recurrence were younger (mean age: 51.3 vs. 52.7 years) and more likely to undergo mastectomy (65.5 vs. 51.7%) than those without recurrence. Recurrence was associated with significantly higher HRU per patient-month (PPM), including breast cancer-related outpatient visits (incidence rate ratio [IRR]: 3.58; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 3.09-4.17), imaging/laboratory testing (IRR: 3.40; 95% CI: 2.77-4.20), emergency department visits (IRR: 3.05; 95% CI: 1.08-6.63), and all-cause hospitalizations (IRR: 2.78; 95% CI: 1.70-4.54). Patients with recurrence also incurred higher monthly all-cause (cost difference [CD]: $15,517; 95% CI: $11,680-$19,991) and breast cancer-related costs (CD: $15,101; 95% CI: $11,275-$19,580), as well as greater work loss PPM (IRR: 2.20; 95% CI: 1.31-3.93) and higher indirect monthly costs (CD: $554; 95% CI: $176-$1,148). LIMITATIONS: Recurrence identified using claims-based proxies may have been under-ascertained or misclassified because claims data lacked detailed clinical characteristics. Follow-up was relatively short. Findings may not generalize to uninsured or non-commercially insured patients. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with high-risk early-stage TNBC treated with NACT and surgery, recurrence was associated with greater HRU, direct costs, and productivity loss. These findings underscore the substantial economic burden associated with recurrence.

title: Proximal policy optimization with adaptive fuzzy logic (PPO-AFL) for high-efficiency maximum power point tracking in three-phase grid-connected photovoltaic systems
abstract: In this work, a new controller called Proximal Policy Optimization with Adaptive Fuzzy Logic (PPO-AFL) is introduced for Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) in a 4.98 kW three-phase grid-connected photovoltaic (PV) system. All testing was done through MATLAB R2023b/Simulink. The PPO-AFL controller links a PPO reinforcement learning agent with Generalized Advantage Estimation (GAE) to a two-timescale Takagi-Sugeno-Kang (TSK) Adaptive Fuzzy Logic (AFL) unit. This setup adjusts the fuzzy membership function parameters in real time without needing any labelled training data. A combined reward signal simultaneously addresses maximum-power extraction, DC-link voltage regulation, grid-current harmonic distortion, and duty-cycle smoothness. The grid-side terms are evaluated against selected harmonic-distortion and power-factor criteria used as power-quality reference limits; full IEEE 1547–2018 compliance is not claimed. Under idealized MATLAB/Simulink simulation conditions, results indicate a steady-state tracking efficiency of 99.5%, a settling time of 52 ms, a power ripple of ± 3 W, a grid current THD of 0.8%, and a power factor of 0.998. These values are better than ten reference algorithms including P&O (92.1%), INC (93.6%), ANN-MPPT (97.3%), and DDPG-MPPT (97.9%) across all measured criteria. An ablation study with five system variants confirms that each component adds independently to the final performance. Statistical tests across 150 simulation runs per algorithm (1,650 observations across the eleven methods; one-way ANOVA, F(10, 1639) = 1124.7, p < 0.001) confirm the findings are significant. Hardware tests such as HIL, PIL, and DSP/FPGA prototype work are needed in future to verify these results in real conditions.

title: IOT Based Monitoring Of CT Scanner Performance And Equipment Safety
journal: International Journal of Creative and Open Research in Engineering and Management
abstract: CT scanners are an essential diagnostic imaging modality that uses x-rays to acquire cross-sectional images. Consistent performance from the system and routine quality control will guarantee the safety and reliability of operation of this equipment. Any problems will be able to be spotted in advance with the help of routine maintenance and checking of radiation-related parameters. Conventional methods of monitoring will include routine testing, logging of data and reporting. However, there could be problems that arise between the routine checks of the equipment. This paper proposes a framework for monitoring CT scanners based on IoT technology. In the process, non-invasive data such as the temperature and humidity of the room where the equipment is installed, equipment status, run time, error codes, cooling system, and selected parameters of quality control will be collected. The information will be uploaded to a server or cloud dashboard through a secure gateway which will allow monitoring of the thresholds, trends and alerting about the unusual parameters. The framework will also allow registering maintenance problems, escalation of the alerts and reviews by Radiographers, Service Engineers, and Medical Physicists. A descriptive design-based methodology will be applied for identifying which parameters will be measured, sensor and data configuration, alert systems creation, security features and evaluation of this framework. As this paper does not include any clinical or equipment testing, the results chapter of this paper will discuss outputs that would be expected from this framework and evaluation of the framework. This framework needs to be used as an additional tool for manufacturer guidance, statutory safety guidelines, acceptance testing or quality control program managed by certified specialists. The use of this IoT framework might improve equipment availability, early detection of problems, better documentation and safer CT services. Keywords— Internet of Things , CT Scanner, Real-Time Monitoring, Equipment Monitoring, Predictive Maintenance, Sensor Technology, Fault Detection.

title: Understanding the Correctional Nursing Workforce: A Comparative Analysis of Wisconsin Registered Nurses
The Role of Nurses in Addressing Climate-Driven Mental Health Challenges: A Narrative Review
abstract: Background: Climate change is one of the most critical public health challenge. Exposure to extreme weather events can lead to anxiety, depression, post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), eco-anxiety, ecological grief, and suicidal ideation. Nurses as frontline community-based professionals, play a vital role in addressing climate-driven mental health impacts. Aim/Objectives: Aims to explore the roles and challenges of nurses in addressing mental health impacts associated with climate change. The specific objectives are: (1)to identify the climate driven mental health challenges (2) to examine nursing interventions for supporting affected individuals, and (3) to identify barriers influencing nurses’ ability to respond effectively. Methods: The literature search was conducted using PubMed, Google Scholar, CINAHL, PsycINFO and Scopus. A purposive sampling technique was applied. Inclusion criteria were: (i) empirical studies, reviews, commentaries that reported mental health related to climate events (ii) explicit description of nurses’ roles, interventions. The quality of the included studies was assessed by considering study design, clarity of objectives, and relevance to the review question. After title and abstract screening, 10 were excluded due to irrelevance. A final total of 08 articles was included based on full-text review. Findings: Nurses play a central role in screening, providing psychoeducation, engaging with the community, building resilience, and advocating for patients. Barriers to effective nursing responses included limited climate- and mental‑health‑specific content in nursing curricula, scarce resources and staffing during climate emergencies, lack of standardized protocols and emotional burden and burnout among nurses. Conclusions and Recommendations: Nurses are pivotal in mitigating climate‑driven mental health challenges through early identification, holistic care, community engagement, and advocacy. Future research should focus on evaluating specific nurse-led interventions for eco-anxiety, ecological grief, and disaster‑related distress.

title: A Five-Phase Participatory Model for Primary Health Care Strategic Planning by Provincial Administrative Organizations: Evidence from Two Pilot Provinces in Northeastern Thailand
abstract: Background: Since 2021, Thailand has transferred sub-district health promotion hospitals (SHPHs) from the Ministry of Public Health to Provincial Administrative Organizations (PAOs). PAOs must now prepare their primary health care (PHC) strategic plans, yet no participatory planning model designed and field-tested for PAOs has been reported. Objectives: To develop a five-phase participatory PHC strategic planning model for PAOs and to assess its workability for implementation during one planning cycle in two provinces with contrasting contexts. Methods: A research and development (R&D) study with an explanatory sequential mixed-methods design was conducted from March 2025 to March 2026 in two purposively selected PAOs in northeastern Thailand: Nong Bua Lam Phu (83 SHPHs, 6 districts) and Sakon Nakhon (149 SHPHs, 18 districts). Participants were planning committee members (n = 78), SHPH directors (232 invited to district SWOT workshops; 132 completed a situation survey), and key informants (n = 24). Three experts content-validated the model (S-CVI = 0.92). We assessed feasibility with a 24-item, six-dimension questionnaire (CVI = 0.89). We analyzed quantitative data descriptively and qualitative data thematically and integrated the two strands during interpretation. Results: SFAS analysis placed Nong Bua Lam Phu in a marginally aggressive position ((S+O)-(W+T) = +0.06) and Sakon Nakhon in a defensive position (-0.94). Nong Bua Lam Phu adopted six strategic areas and 31 KPIs (reduced from 95 candidates); Sakon Nakhon adopted four strategic areas and 28 KPIs (from 68). All final KPIs met the SMART criteria. The two PAOs produced 17 projects and 59 activities. Both provinces rated the perceived feasibility of implementing the plans as good (M = 3.75 and 3.97 out of 5), with the economic dimension rated lowest. Sakon Nakhon incorporated its plan into the fiscal year 2027 (B.E. 2570) budget ordinance. Conclusion: The five-phase model was feasible to implement within a normal annual planning cycle and produced plans that differed according to each province's strategic position. The study did not assess its effects on service delivery and health outcomes; longer-term evaluation in more provinces is needed before wider adoption. Keywords: strategic health planning, health decentralization, Provincial Administrative Organization, primary health care, participatory planning, Thailand

title: Digitally Enabled Hybrid Delivery of HIV Preexposure Prophylaxis in Gauteng Province, South Africa: Mixed Methods Feasibility and Acceptability Study
abstract: Background Facility-based preexposure prophylaxis (PrEP) services often deter potential users through privacy and stigma concerns, travel requirements, waiting times, and restricted operating hours. Digital models may help address some of these barriers, but evidence on hybrid digital and telemedicine PrEP pathways for general adult populations in African settings remains limited. Objective This study aims to assess the feasibility and acceptability of a digitally enabled hybrid oral PrEP delivery pathway combining digital engagement and HIV self-testing (HIVST) with home-based nurse assessment, virtual physician prescribing, pharmacist dispensing, courier delivery of medication, and HIVST-supported follow-up in Gauteng province, South Africa. Methods We used a multiphase mixed methods design. In May 2023, 127 adults recruited through convenience sampling via an online platform and community pharmacies participating in the PPREPP-SA (Pharmacy-Delivered Preexposure Prophylaxis in South Africa) implementation project in Johannesburg and Cape Town completed a market survey. In June 2023, study staff invited adults who were available and willing to participate at pharmacies in both cities; 30 completed formative interviews, which were analyzed descriptively. During implementation (July 2023-July 2024), users self-enrolled through the online platform, and website analytics and programmatic data described progression to PrEP initiation (n=155). At 6 to 7 months—the midpoint of the 13-month follow-up period—criterion-based purposive sampling was used to select users from 3 engagement groups: active, missed appointment, and lost to follow-up. Seven users completed midline interviews. In addition, one senior manager from the online platform completed a key informant interview. Preimplementation interviews were analyzed descriptively, midline interviews were analyzed thematically, and findings were integrated using a joint display. Results Among the 127 market survey respondents, 96 (75.6%) preferred pharmacy-based PrEP, whereas 17 (13.4%) selected online access; 83 (65.4%) were willing to pay for PrEP-related services. During implementation, 567 users ordered an HIV self-test, 457 (80.6%) received it, 253 reported a nonreactive result, 192 requested a nurse visit, 157 completed the visit, and 155 initiated PrEP. Initiation represented 61.3% (155/253) of users reporting a nonreactive result and 27.3% (155/567) of all users who ordered a test. Among the 155 participants who initiated PrEP, 97 (62.6%) were assigned male at birth, 123 (79.4%) had tertiary education, and 110 (70.9%) were employed. Privacy, discretion, and convenience supported acceptability. The absence of clearly identifiable addresses, courier delivery and laboratory delays, scheduling difficulties, and communication breakdowns between participants and study staff affected progression through the pathway. Participants and the platform stakeholder also raised concerns about affordability, poststudy access, and financial sustainability. Conclusions The digitally enabled hybrid PrEP pathway supported PrEP initiation among users who valued privacy and convenience. Its feasibility was conditional on coordination among multiple service components. Wider implementation will require streamlined clinical and logistical processes, equitable digital access, flexible delivery or collection options, and sustainable financing that complements existing pharmacy- and facility-based PrEP services.

title: Mobile Health for Biomedical and Economic Intelligence: An Integrated Adoption Model for Young Adults
journal: International Journal of Online and Biomedical Engineering (iJOE)
abstract: Mobile health (m-health) has become an important component of digital healthcare delivery, yet its long-term value depends not only on technical usability but also on user adoption patterns that influence scalability, resource efficiency, and sustainable service design. Using a hybrid of Theory of Planned Behaviour (TPB), the technology acceptance model (TAM), Dual Factor Theory, and trust, we developed a model to examine the determinants of m-health adoption among young adults in Asia during and post-COVID-19. Our evidence is based on an online survey of 390 respondents aged 20–39 who reported that behavioural, technological, and psychological factors shape adoption intentions and reflect on biomedical intelligence and personalised treatment plans. Variables such as attitude and subjective norm were found to be most influential on the adoption decision for m-health services. Systems trust and resistance to change also enhanced the rate of adoption. Attitude emerges as the most significant factor, while perceived ease of use and perceived usefulness exert indirect effects on attitude. Subjective norm, trust, and resistance to change significantly impact the perceived usefulness for both users and healthcare providers. Based on these results, it can be stated that increasing trust, focusing on users’ needs and values, and developing cost-efficient and personalised m-health solutions are key elements. Our study also confirms that system trust enhances the biomedical intelligence, early diagnosis of fatal diseases, and biomedical innovation.

title: Diverse ‘rurals’: comparing mainland and island-dwelling older adults’ perceptions of formal care
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Care in rural and remote areas is often characterised as problematic, yet this framing can obscure important differences between rural places and the factors driving these. Few studies compare perceptions of formal care recipients between different rural locations. This article contrasts older adults' views of a range of care services - including primary, secondary, and social care - across island and mainland rural sites. METHODS: The study draws on 14 months of ethnographic fieldwork conducted in two locations: 'Insh', a remote island located off the west coast of Scotland; and 'Willow Valley', an area encompassing three villages in the northern English county of Cumbria. Data were collected through participant observation in community settings and semi-structured interviews. A total of 36 participants were interviewed, comprising 33 older adults aged 66-92 years and three family members involved in care. Participants were recruited via community groups and snowball sampling. Interviews were conducted in participants' homes, transcribed verbatim, and analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. RESULTS: The findings demonstrate clear contrasts in perceptions of care between the two sites. On Insh, participants generally reported positive experiences, particularly in relation to on-island care. Access to healthcare professionals, especially GPs, was described as timely and straightforward. Perceptions were linked by participants to a local 'diseconomy of scale', which supported the maintenance of services despite the island's small population, but also to the broader social geography of the island. Repeated encounters in everyday spaces and the circulation of information through gossip networks meant that residents came to know, and be known by, those involved in delivering their care. These dynamics generated not only practical benefits such as continuity of care but also a broader sense of security and trust. Although participants also identified specific challenges, including difficulties with emergency transport, the need to travel for secondary care, and limitations in aspects of social care provision, overall evaluations of care were favourable. In contrast, participants in Willow Valley described more negative and uncertain experiences, particularly in relation to lesser accessibility and continuity of primary care. Difficulties in securing appointments, reliance on telephone triage, and a loss of continuity with clinicians were reported. While concerns were shared with participants living in Insh regarding travel to secondary care and the availability of social care, more spatially dispersed social relations meant that care providers were less embedded within local community life. This resulted in more fragmented and uncertain perceptions of care. CONCLUSION: Perceptions of formal health and social care can vary significantly across rural areas, challenging 'deficit' framings. There is a need for place-sensitive approaches to policy that recognise differences both between and within island and mainland rural settings.

title: Frailty-stratified stepped cardiac rehabilitation and cardiovascular outcomes after primary PCI in elderly patients: a propensity-score-matched cohort study
abstract: Background Frailty is common among older survivors of acute myocardial infarction (AMI) and shapes both the hazards and the gains of cardiac rehabilitation; yet, conventional programmes apply one fixed intensity to all. We examined whether grading rehabilitation intensity to the Fried frailty phenotype is associated with better cardiovascular outcomes. Methods In a single-centre retrospective cohort study, consecutive patients aged ≥65 years discharged alive after primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for AMI between January 2016 and December 2021 received either a frailty-stratified stepped rehabilitation pathway, allocated by physician referral (n = 253), or usual care (n = 233). After 1:1 propensity-score matching (202 pairs), the primary outcome was 12-month major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Sensitivity analyses included inverse-probability weighting, doubly robust estimation, a time-dependent exposure model, a 30-day landmark analysis, and a pre-specified subgroup aged ≥75 years. A Fine–Gray model addressed competing risks for readmission. Results After matching, 12-month MACE occurred in 17.8% (stepped) versus 24.8% (usual care). The crude hazard ratio (HR) was 0.69 (95% CI 0.45–1.06; P = 0.092), and statistical significance was reached only after multivariable adjustment (adjusted HR 0.62, 0.40–0.95; P = 0.030). All seven Cox-based sensitivity estimates were below 1.0, but only two were statistically significant (time-dependent HR 0.66, 0.44–0.98; landmark HR 0.63, 0.40–0.99); adjustment for all residually imbalanced covariates gave HR 0.65 (0.42–1.01; P = 0.055). The E -value was 2.13 (1.23 for the confidence limit). In exploratory analyses by frailty stratum, estimates were imprecise and the treatment-by-frailty interaction was not significant (P = 0.57). All-cause readmission was lower (26.7% vs. 36.6%; adjusted OR 0.59, 0.39–0.92; Fine–Gray sub-distribution HR 0.65, 0.44–0.97). The stepped pathway was also associated with longer 6-minute walk distance (+28 m, P < 0.001), higher SF-36 physical component scores (+4.5, P < 0.001), and higher rehabilitation adherence (+10.7 percentage points, P < 0.001). Conclusions In elderly post-PCI patients, a frailty-stratified stepped rehabilitation pathway was associated with fewer readmissions and better functional recovery than usual care. Its association with lower 12-month MACE was model-dependent and may partly reflect residual selection bias; it should be regarded as hypothesis-generating pending confirmation in a randomised trial.

title: Clinical text de-identification with locally deployed open-weight large language models: a real-world evaluation of discharge notes
abstract: Background Clinical notes contain protected health information, which can restrict their sharing and reuse in research. Manual de-identification is time-consuming and difficult to scale. Locally deployed open-weight large language models (LLMs) can process sensitive text without transmitting data to external model services, but their performance in removing identifiers from real-world discharge notes remains uncertain. Methods We evaluated 17 locally deployed open-weight LLMs on 100 real-world discharge notes in a study approved by the Institutional Review Board. Two reviewers trained in Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) requirements independently annotated the discharge notes and resolved disagreements by consensus, creating a consensus reference standard of 3,537 identifier spans. Each model processed every note in two sequential passes using a locked system prompt, user prompt template, and study-specific 18-category output schema based on HIPAA Safe Harbor; the complete evaluation was executed three times under these locked settings. The only comparator was Microsoft Presidio, an untuned, general-purpose personally identifiable information tool. We measured character recall, redaction outside the reference spans, identifier-boundary accuracy, note-level completeness, the incremental contribution of the second pass, and processing time. Results After two passes, character recall ranged from 39.6% to 98.9% across models; the six highest-recall models achieved 95.0% to 98.9%, with Gemma-4 31B having the highest observed recall. The highest reported mean note-level completeness was 67 of 100 notes, rounded across three executions. Residual characters occurred in both untouched and partially removed reference spans. The second pass increased recall by up to 15.0 percentage points. Median two-pass processing time ranged from 14.1 to 740.2 s per note. Conclusion Several locally deployed open-weight LLMs achieved high character recall, although redaction selectivity and processing time varied widely. High pooled recall coexisted with incomplete removal of reference-identifier characters within individual notes. These outcomes measure removal against the reference annotations and do not determine whether residual text remains identifying. The study does not establish suitability for autonomous release of clinical text or an advantage over optimized or supervised clinical de-identification tools.

title: Patterns of disease burden and healthcare availability across rural and urban settings in selected local government areas of Enugu State, Nigeria
abstract: Many communities in southeastern Nigeria face a simultaneous burden of communicable and non-communicable diseases, yet evidence linking disease patterns with healthcare availability across rural and urban settings remains limited. This study assessed the pattern of disease burden and healthcare availability in selected rural and urban communities of Enugu State, Nigeria. A cross-sectional mixed-methods study was conducted among 402 adults selected through multistage sampling from four local government areas, with the household survey and focus group discussions drawn from the same rural and urban communities. Hospital records comprising 620 patient cases were reviewed separately, at facilities serving these communities, to describe disease profiles and treatment outcomes rather than to estimate population-level prevalence. Quantitative data were analysed using descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and binary logistic regression at a 5% level of significance, while qualitative data underwent thematic analysis, with the two strands brought together at the interpretation stage. Malaria ( n = 286; 46.1%) was the most frequently documented diagnosis in hospital records, followed by hypertension ( n = 214; 34.5%) and typhoid fever ( n = 173; 27.9%), indicating the coexistence of communicable and non-communicable diseases in this facility-based sample. Although 334 of 402 respondents (83.0%) reported that a health facility existed within their community, substantial proportions identified challenges with medicine availability ( n = 160; 39.8%), affordability ( n = 145; 36.1%), and physical accessibility ( n = 130; 32.3%); these items formed part of a broader composite healthcare availability score distinct from simple facility presence. On this composite score, healthcare availability showed only a borderline, non-significant difference by residence, with urban respondents reporting high availability somewhat more often than rural respondents (131 of 232, 56.5%, versus 79 of 169, 46.7%; χ² = 3.703, p = 0.054). After adjustment for sociodemographic covariates, urban residence was independently associated with lower odds of high disease burden (AOR = 0.33, 95% CI: 0.13 to 0.84, reference category rural), younger adults and those aged 50 to 59 years also carried significantly greater odds of high disease burden than respondents aged 60 and above, and male sex independently predicted lower odds of high healthcare availability than female sex (AOR = 0.61, 95% CI: 0.38 to 0.97). Hospital record review found that 214 of 620 patients (34.5%) were referred, 208 (33.5%) were discharged as recovered, 25 (4.0%) died during admission, and 173 (27.9%) had no treatment documented in the record, a category that spans discharge against medical advice, apparent medicine stock-outs, and gaps in documentation rather than confirmed absence of care. Enugu State continues to experience a concurrent burden of communicable and non-communicable diseases alongside marked rural-urban inequalities in healthcare availability. Improving the readiness of rural primary healthcare facilities, ensuring reliable supplies of essential medicines, strengthening referral systems, and reducing financial and geographic barriers to care may help narrow this gap, although the cross-sectional design cannot establish that these steps would directly improve health outcomes.

title: Informal Customer Relationship Management in B2B Healthcare Distribution: Empirical Insights from a Small Medical Consumables Distributor in India
Temporal stability of opportunistic infection reporting patterns in kidney transplantation
abstract: Background Opportunistic infections (OIs) after kidney transplantation occur within complex treatment and host-defense contexts. Spontaneous reports retain several events within each record. We examined whether pathogen-related reporting vocabulary remained stable over time after accounting for report complexity, event frequencies and the OI-entry definition. Methods We analyzed US Food and Drug Administration Adverse Event Reporting System reports from 2004Q1 to 2026Q2. Kidney-transplant indications linked to the same primary- or secondary-suspect immunosuppressant identified 31,004 reports, including 4,123 with prespecified OI terms. Development reports (n=3,264; through 2022Q4) informed feature construction and forward-chaining selection of non-negative matrix factorization models with 2–12 components. The selected basis was projected into 859 later reports by non-negative least squares. Evaluation included degree-preserving and OI-conditioned randomization, alternative models, calendar shuffling, source restrictions, and renal-context ablation. Modified Poisson models estimated adjusted reporting-prevalence ratios (aRPRs), with false-discovery-rate correction. Two assessors independently reviewed 200 reports. Sensitivity analyses examined alternative component numbers, shared terminology, suspected duplicate reports, date availability and the choice of drug-start date. Exposure models retained overlapping drug indicators and explicit within-reporting-frame reference groups. Later-period exposure and event counts characterized support for each coefficient. Results Eleven components were selected, with a median random-initialization adjusted Rand index of 0.865. Later-period median reconstruction cosine was 0.497 (95% confidence interval, 0.484–0.509). The degree-preserving null median was 0.426; additionally preserving each report’s OI-term count increased it to 0.474 (2.5th–97.5th percentiles, 0.464–0.484; observed-minus-null difference, 0.023; Monte Carlo p=0.001). PCA achieved cosine 0.520, and the chronological score fell within the calendar-shuffle distribution. Binary coding yielded 0.613. All five suspect-drug indicators were associated with OI-entry reporting (aRPRs, 1.121–2.772). CNI, belatacept and mTOR indicators were associated with coded death; no hospitalization association remained significant after multiplicity correction. Drug-start-to-event intervals were available for 776 reports (18.8%). The unweighted median was 82.5 days; expanded availability weighting yielded 93 days. Agreement on coded OI evidence was 98.0%. Conclusion Degree-conditioned pathogen vocabulary was stable across calendar periods in kidney-transplant OI-entry reports. The components provide descriptive summaries of submitted reports and focused questions for studies with clinical infection and immune measurements.

title: Investigation of Sources of Bias in Healthcare AI in South Korea
journal: International Journal of Online and Biomedical Engineering (iJOE)
abstract: South Korea is expanding the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in healthcare through large-scale healthcare data initiatives. As AI increasingly relies on medical datasets, concerns have emerged regarding potential bias. This study aims to examine how existing inequalities in South Korea may contribute to potential bias in healthcare AI and to identify the major factors that influence the representativeness of medical datasets. The research was conducted using academic articles, government reports, and news sources related to healthcare, digital technology, and AI in South Korea. The analysis focuses on five potential sources of healthcare AI bias: age and digital literacy, gender, socioeconomic status, regional healthcare disparities, and structural limitations of healthcare databases. Existing social and structural inequalities may influence the representativeness of healthcare data used to develop AI systems. Older adults may be underrepresented due to lower digital literacy and reduced use of digital health technologies. Gender differences in disease prevalence, symptom presentation, healthcare utilization, and medication use may contribute to unequal data representation. Socioeconomic and regional disparities may further affect healthcare access and data generation, while limitations of national health insurance databases may influence data quality and completeness.

title: Multistakeholder Expectations and Implementation Concerns Regarding AI-Based Pregnancy Risk Assessment in Maternity Care: Qualitative Descriptive Study
abstract: Background Pregnancy risk assessment requires not only accurate identification of risk but also communication, referral, and follow-up across different levels of care. Although AI-based tools are increasingly proposed to support this process, evidence remains limited on how women, primary health care professionals, and hospital-based maternity care providers expect AI-generated risk information to be interpreted and used in care, as well as on what conditions they consider important for its practical use. Objective This study aimed to explore multistakeholder expectations and anticipated implementation concerns regarding AI-based pregnancy risk assessment in maternity care, with particular attention to how AI-generated risk information could be interpreted, confirmed, and used to inform care decisions and subsequent management. Methods This qualitative descriptive study used semistructured interviews with 93 participants in Guizhou Province, China, including 33 (33.5%) pregnant or postpartum women, 23 (24.7%) primary health care professionals, and 37 (39.8%) hospital-based maternity care providers. Purposive sampling with maximum variation was used. Participants were recruited from 18 health care facilities, including primary health care facilities and secondary and tertiary hospitals. Interviews were conducted between August 30, 2024, and May 2026. Brief standardized conceptual material was used to support discussion of AI-based pregnancy risk assessment; it did not depict a specific product or prototype. Data were analyzed using inductive qualitative content analysis. Results Five descriptive themes and 16 subthemes were developed. The expected value of AI-based pregnancy risk assessment depended on whether it addressed practical gaps in pregnancy risk management, although priorities differed across stakeholder groups. Women emphasized understandable risk information and care-seeking guidance; primary health care professionals emphasized referral, feedback, and follow-up continuity; and hospital-based providers valued clinically interpretable information for assessment, management, and cross-level coordination. Participants valued early and dynamic risk recognition because pregnancy risk could emerge, worsen, or be reclassified as pregnancy progressed, making sustained visibility of risk information important. AI-generated risk information was not treated as self-evident; it needed to be interpreted and confirmed in relation to women’s bodily experience, clinicians’ judgment, examination results, referral rules, and higher-level confirmation. Risk recognition was considered useful when it could be translated into guidance, referral, feedback, and follow-up. Implementation concerns centered on risk communication and anxiety management for women and on workload, usability, training, and organizational support for health care professionals. Conclusions Stakeholders expected AI-based pregnancy risk assessment to provide risk information that could become meaningful and actionable within existing maternity care pathways. Future AI tools in maternity care should therefore be evaluated not only for predictive accuracy but also for whether risk information can be understood, communicated, confirmed, and carried forward into follow-up and coordinated action across levels of care.

title: Healthcare Provider and Patient Perspectives on Comprehensive Hepatitis B Prevention and Control: A Qualitative Study in Central urban area of Shanghai, China
abstract: Background The burden of chronic hepatitis B (CHB) in China remains significant. There are still numerous practical shortcomings in clinical diagnosis and treatment, grassroots prevention and control, patients' health awareness, and hierarchical referral. This study, from the perspectives of both service providers and demanders, analyzes the current status and actual service needs of CHB prevention and control in the central urban area of Shanghai, providing a practical basis for optimizing the refined management of hepatitis B in the region. Methods From February to May 2025, 20 healthcare service providers and 22 patients with CHB were recruited. Using stratified purposive sampling, we selected medical workers from the health administrative management department, disease control center, and hospitals at all levels. As well as included patients of different disease courses, follow-up compliance, age, and gender characteristics as the research subjects. Following the principle of information saturation in qualitative research. The data collected through a pair of semi-structured interviews were analyzed using thematic research guided by the translational medicine framework (T2–T4). Results We found that particularly older patients, have misconceptions and information gaps, which contributes to poor treatment adherence. The professional competence of grassroots medical workers is insufficient, and staffing levels are inadequate. The two-way referral mechanism is not yet well established, with obstacles including patients' distrust of the grassroots healthcare facilities, shortages of medication at the grassroots level, and inadequate information during the referral process. The chronic liver health management services currently implemented in Shanghai can alleviate patients’ economic burden and improve their quality of life to some extent; however, further improvement is needed. Establishing a disease-specific system that covers the entire continuum of CHB prevention, screening, diagnosis, and treatment can enhance efficiency and promote standardized management. Conclusions In the future, efforts should be made to explore multi-disease prevention and service innovation models, strengthen health education and psychological intervention. Improve supporting measures and grassroots services, deepen the integration of medical care and prevention, and establish a complete chain of CHB prevention, screening, diagnosis, follow-up, and psychological support.

title: Effects of continuity of midwifery care on intrapartum referral, maternal and perinatal outcomes, and women's experiences
abstract: INTRODUCTION: The Dutch maternity care system is characterized by a fragmented structure with frequent transfers from primary to secondary care. These transfers may disrupt continuity of care and negatively affect women's experiences. This study evaluated an integrated maternity care model in which community midwives retained responsibility for intrapartum care of women with mild medical indications within a hospital setting. MATERIAL AND METHODS: A quasi-experimental non-equivalent groups design was used in Amsterdam Southeast, the Netherlands, a socioeconomically and ethnically diverse urban area. In total, 413 women with singleton pregnancies receiving care from community midwifery practices consented to participation: 261 before and 152 after introduction of the integrated care model. Of these, 53 before (controls) and 33 after introduction (intervention) met the criteria for intrapartum care by a community midwife within integrated care pathways. Of these 33 women (after introduction), nine (27%) actually received our Follow Mom model. Before introduction, community midwives had not yet been trained; these women served as the control group. The primary outcome was the Adverse Outcome Index-5 (AOI-5). Secondary outcomes included maternal, neonatal, and care process and patient-reported experience outcomes. RESULTS: Among eligible women, the AOI-5 did not differ significantly between the control and intervention group (OR 0.78, 95% CI: 0.21-2.81). No differences were observed in maternal or neonatal outcomes, including postpartum hemorrhage, severe perineal trauma, NICU admission, or Apgar score <7 at 5 min. Women were less likely to be referred to secondary care during labor in the intervention group (OR 0.26, 95% CI 0.09-0.80). Patient-reported experience measures were high in both groups (82.1% vs. 93.8%). CONCLUSIONS: Following introduction of the integrated maternity care model, fewer intrapartum referrals were observed, without differences in clinical outcomes. Although small numbers, these findings suggest that enhanced collaboration between primary and secondary care may reduce fragmentation of maternity care without an observed increase in adverse maternal or neonatal outcomes.

title: Association between specialized outpatient care and patient-reported primary care experience among patients with chronic diseases in Shanghai: a cross-sectional study
abstract: Specialized outpatient care has been introduced in Chinese community health service centres to strengthen chronic disease management. However, whether this model is associated with more favourable patient-reported primary care experience remains unclear. This study compared primary care experiences between patients attending specialized outpatient clinics and general outpatient clinics in Shanghai. A multistage cross-sectional survey was conducted from June to October 2024 among patients with chronic diseases who attended community health service centres in Shanghai where specialized outpatient care models had been implemented. Participants were recruited from either specialized outpatient clinics for specific chronic diseases or general outpatient clinics. Patient-reported primary care experience was assessed using the Primary Care Assessment Tool–Adult Short version. Analysis of variance was used to compare characteristics and primary care experience scores between groups. Multivariable linear regression was performed to identify factors associated with the total primary care experience score. A total of 581 valid questionnaires were included in the analysis. Compared with patients attending general outpatient clinics, those attending specialized outpatient clinics reported significantly higher scores across all primary care experience domains and a higher total Primary Care Assessment Tool–Adult Short version score. In multivariable linear regression analysis, attending a specialized outpatient clinic was positively associated with the total primary care experience score after adjustment for patient characteristics and health-related factors ( β = 0.195 , P < 0.001 ). Other factors independently associated with higher total scores included age ≥ 71 years ( β = 0.179 , P < 0.001 ), awareness of the harms associated with chronic diseases ( β = 0.166 , P < 0.001 ), and receiving disease-related health education from attending physicians or family doctors ( β = 0.181 , P < 0.001 ). In this cross-sectional study, attendance at a specialized outpatient clinic was associated with more favourable patient-reported primary care experiences among patients with diabetes or COPD. However, the cross-sectional design and potential residual confounding preclude causal inference. Further improvement is needed in referral coordination and community-oriented care, and longitudinal multicentre studies are warranted to evaluate the broader effectiveness of this service model.

title: Clinic vs. Screen: Comparing Fully In-Person to Virtual-Plus–In-Person Cardiac Fitness and Rehabilitation Programs for Congenital Heart Disease
abstract: Cardiac fitness and rehabilitation programs offer meaningful benefits for individuals with congenital heart disease (CHD), and newer delivery models include hybrid formats combining virtual and in-person training. We hypothesized that the convenience of hybrid delivery would improve program adherence and patient satisfaction while remaining safe and effective compared with in-person training alone. In this retrospective cohort study of 158 participants with CHD (68 in-person, 90 hybrid), groups were similar at baseline, including distance traveled, except for sex (p = 0.035) and hemodynamic level (p = 0.002). Both groups demonstrated significant pre- to post-program improvements in aerobic capacity, strength, and flexibility, with few between-group differences and no adverse events. Psychologic outcomes favored the hybrid group, with greater gains in self-efficacy (p = 0.017) and larger reductions in parent-reported patient anxiety (p = 0.02). A trend toward greater fitness progression from entry to advanced level was seen in the hybrid group (32% vs. 21%), though not reaching statistical significance. Contrary to our hypothesis, adherence was comparable between groups (median 19 vs. 16 sessions, p = 0.15). Satisfaction was high for both (93% vs. 97%, p = 0.74), though notably, among hybrid participants completing both session types, in-person was preferred (p < 0.001). Thus, each delivery model produced meaningful, safe fitness improvements in patients with CHD. Hybrid delivery achieved benefits comparable to, or exceeding, fully in-person programming, yet in-person sessions were preferred and did not sacrifice adherence, suggesting direct social connection is valued. As the field moves toward technology-enabled delivery, these findings support flexible models integrating virtual training while preserving social connection.

title: Optimising Oxygen Orders: A Quality Improvement Project of Oxygen Prescription for Patients in a Tertiary Acute Medical Unit in London
abstract: Introduction Oxygen should be regarded as a drug, and indeed is the most common drug administered during medical emergencies. Best practice is to prescribe oxygen for all patients admitted to hospital, to allow for prompt administration and for saturation titration in the event of deterioration and increased oxygen requirement. This is especially pertinent for patients at risk of hypercapnic respiratory failure. Current practices at our hospital, however, did not follow this recommendation, despite clear visual reminders both physically and digitally, which resulted in a clinical need our quality improvement project aimed to fulfil Methods One hundred patients admitted to a tertiary acute medical unit over 2 weeks had their oxygen prescription use audited within their first 24 hours of admission. Then, via a Plan-Do-Study-Act (PDSA) methodology, a further new cohort of 25 patients was re-audited following awareness and teaching sessions, followed by a final 25 patients using both teaching sessions and direct reminders consistently. Results Oxygen prescription rates were below expected, at 1% pre-intervention of the total 100 patients audited. This is despite every wall-mounted oxygen valve having a historic prompt, ‘is oxygen prescribed?’, and our electronic prescribing system having a summary page with a field for the oxygen prescription in plain view. Discussions with the team revealed a lack of awareness around the need for oxygen prescriptions, and a lack of importance placed on it when oxygen was readily available from wall outlets and need not be signed out by the nursing team. Following a teaching session in the handover, supplemented by direct reminders in the second cycle, oxygen prescription rates increased to 28% (n=25) in the first re-audit, then 48% (n=25) in the final, and 50% in those requiring oxygen (n=12). Conclusion Visual reminders may be ignored and become part of background noise rather than a prompt for change in practice. Further methods are needed to optimise oxygen prescription rather than these alone, such as teaching sessions and direct reminders. Many current oxygen audits observe adherence directly post-intervention but may not offer a long-term perspective or solution once teaching sessions/visual reminders are completed and/or forgotten. Indeed, one benefit of an electronic system may be a hard stop - an option we are currently exploring to maintain and improve compliance with oxygen prescribing.

title: From improvement to intensification: a framework of the dark side of continuous improvement in healthcare
Cardiovascular health metrics and risk models in population eye care: evidence and clinical utility
abstract: Cardiovascular information collected in primary care may help identify individuals who could benefit from eye assessment or additional screening support. This Mini Review examines human evidence linking composite cardiovascular health scores and cardiovascular event-risk models to ocular outcomes, based on literature searches updated through 8 November 2026. Life's Simple 7 and Life's Essential 8 summarize cardiovascular health, whereas the Pooled Cohort Equations (PCE) estimate cardiovascular event risk. More favorable cardiovascular health profiles have been associated with lower odds of prevalent retinopathy and lower incidence of retinal vein occlusion and age-related macular degeneration. However, associations with composite microvascular outcomes may not extend to diabetic retinopathy (DR) specifically. In the All of Us study, adjusted models incorporating PCE-defined risk showed discrimination for selected ocular outcomes; comparable models without PCE were not reported. Evaluation should therefore compare established ocular predictors alone, predictors supplemented by cardiovascular composites, and models incorporating their constituent variables. The Individualised Screening for Diabetic Retinopathy trial provides an implementation benchmark for risk-based recall among previously screened patients, whereas prioritizing individuals before their first retinal examination requires a separate approach. The studies reviewed do not establish that adding cardiovascular metrics improves ocular prediction or clinical decisions. Future evaluation should assess predictive performance alongside screening completion, timely referral, resource use, and equitable access to eye care.

title: A review of cancer therapy-related cardiovascular toxicity: mechanisms and pharmacological management
abstract: Cancer therapy-related cardiovascular toxicity includes myocardial dysfunction, ischemia, thrombosis, arrhythmias, and immune-mediated myocarditis, with distinct mechanisms across anticancer treatments. This review integrates evidence published primarily from 2023 to October 2026, building on the 2022 European Society of Cardiology cardio-oncology guideline and International Cardio-Oncology Society consensus. We examine drug-specific injury pathways associated with anthracyclines, other conventional cytotoxic agents (fluoropyrimidines, cyclophosphamide, cisplatin, and taxanes), HER2-directed and other targeted therapies, and immune checkpoint inhibitors; thoracic radiotherapy is addressed briefly for mechanistic comparison. We consider how biomarkers, cardiac imaging, and treatment-related risk assessment may inform cardioprotective decisions without equating early abnormalities with established clinical benefit. A critical comparison of recent trials of neurohormonal antagonists, statins, and sodium–glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors highlights heterogeneous or preliminary findings, reflecting differences in patient selection, intervention timing, and endpoint definitions. We also distinguish emerging molecular targets, pharmacogenomic markers, and artificial intelligence-based prediction from clinically validated interventions. The available evidence supports treatment-specific cardiovascular assessment but remains insufficient to establish the clinical effectiveness of several proposed preventive drugs. Further adequately powered trials should evaluate mechanism-informed, risk-adapted cardioprotection using clinically meaningful cardiovascular outcomes without compromising anticancer efficacy.

title: Older hospitals, better comfort: comparing thermal performance of Zanzibar hospital ward types
journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: This preprint compares the thermal performance of two standardised hospital ward types in Zanzibar: new district hospital wards (built 2023–24) and older "cottage hospital" wards (built 1970s–80s). At Kivunge Hospital, where both types operate side by side, indoor temperature and relative humidity were monitored in six wards and one clinical room from July to August 2025, and thermal comfort was assessed using Predicted Percentage of Dissatisfied (PPD). The older cottage wards were substantially cooler and more comfortable than the new wards (mean PPD 7.8% vs 41.9%). Cooling the new wards with air conditioning to match the cottage wards would cost an estimated USD 23 per bed per month, or around USD 250,000 per year across the 900 beds in Zanzibar's nine new district hospitals. Solar radiation simulations, analysis of drawings and site imagery, and staff interviews identified the design factors behind the difference, including reduced shading, tree clearance, hard landscaping, building orientation and lack of cross-ventilation. The findings highlight the value of integrating passive design early in hospital planning, as healthcare infrastructure in Zanzibar and sub-Saharan Africa expands. This work forms part of the MBD-Free Project. Results were presented at the Global Health Symposium: Extreme heat and health in the context of climate change, Copenhagen, 10–12 December 2025.

title: Residual learning for predicting revisions to hospital reimbursement standards
abstract: Hospital reimbursement standards may be revised after care is delivered, creating financial uncertainty. We developed ResPay, a neural framework that uses residual learning to predict corrections to current standards from a single hospital's clinical and cost records. A jointly trained classifier identifies groups likely to undergo large revisions and enables selective correction. We retrospectively evaluated separate models at two Chinese hospitals on 219 diagnosis-intervention packet (DIP) and 69 diagnosis-related group (DRG) groups withheld from training within each cohort's payment transition. ResPay achieved the highest average precision (0.731 and 0.568, respectively) for identifying large revisions among evaluated methods. It also achieved the lowest mean absolute and root mean squared errors, reducing mean absolute error by 17.27% in DIP and 11.43% in DRG relative to retaining current standards. These exploratory findings support further evaluation of reimbursement forecasting for hospital planning.

title: Penicillin Allergy Delabeling in Hospitals: A Review of Prescribing, Safety, and Implementation
Economic burden of human Mycoplasma pneumoniae infection in Wuhan, China, based on citywide surveillance data in 2023
abstract: Objective Mycoplasma pneumoniae infection remains prevalent in China and imposes a substantial economic burden. This study characterized the economic burden across population groups and healthcare-related factors in Wuhan in 2023. Methods A total of 24,543 Mycoplasma pneumoniae infection cases with complete treatment cost data were included. Descriptive statistics and nonparametric tests were performed to characterize the study population and compare medical costs across subgroups. A generalized linear model (GLM) with a Gamma distribution and log link was used to assess the associations of demographic characteristics, hospital level (Primary & Secondary Hospitals vs. High-level Hospitals), treatment modality, and antimicrobial use with medical costs. Age-specific observed treatment expenditure was calculated for the cost-analysis sample. Population-level LRTI-related DALYs and their productivity-related economic values were estimated separately and were not attributed specifically to MP infection. Results Individuals aged 0–17 years accounted for 84.4% of all reported Mycoplasma pneumoniae infection cases, with the largest number of cases in the 6–11 years age group. The mean treatment cost among included cases was 5,673.20 CNY. The total observed treatment expenditure was the highest among children aged 6–11 years (57.77 million CNY), while the mean cost per case was highest among those aged ≥60 years (7,562.34 CNY). Hospitalization was associated with higher adjusted costs (cost ratio = 1.07, 95% CI: 1.01–1.14). The treatment costs of several younger age groups were significantly lower than that of the ≥60 years group. The GLM results indicated that hospital level and recorded use of macrolides or novel tetracyclines were not significantly associated with treatment costs. LRTI-related DALY burden was highest among individuals aged ≥60 years. Conclusion Mycoplasma pneumoniae infection in Wuhan primarily affected children, while older adults had the highest mean treatment cost per case. Age and hospitalization status were associated with treatment costs. These findings support attention to age-specific healthcare needs and resource allocation. Population-level LRTI estimates should be interpreted separately and cannot be attributed specifically to Mycoplasma pneumoniae infection.

title: Clinical Segregation of Joint Replacement Surgery Between Israel’s Public and Private Hospitals, 2020–2025: A National Analysis of Case- Mix and Its Policy Implications
abstract: Background Israel has a mixed public–private hospital system, and elective joint replacement is increasingly performed in private hospitals. This study describes national trends in procedure volume and Ministry-classified complexity by hospital sector from 2020 to 2025. Methods We analyzed aggregate national data published by the Israeli Ministry of Health for 2020–2025 for total knee replacement (TKR), total hip replacement (THR), and partial hip replacement (PHR). Counts and proportions were summarized descriptively by procedure, sector, year, and the Ministry’s simple/complex classification. No patient-level adjustment or inferential testing was performed. Results National procedure volume increased from 10,764 in 2020 to 15,848 in 2025 (47.2%). Private-hospital volume increased by 93.3%, compared with 24.5% in public hospitals; the private share rose from 33.1% to 43.4%. In 2025, 24.8% of procedures in public hospitals and 1.90% in private hospitals were classified as complex. The difference varied by procedure type and was particularly influenced by partial hip replacements: all complex partial hip replacements reported during the study period were performed in public hospitals. The public-sector complex caseload increased from 1,614 to 2,227 procedures. Conclusions The aggregate data show a substantial and persistent difference in the distribution of Ministry-classified complexity between hospital sectors. They do not establish whether the difference reflects provider selection, patient choice, referral practices, differences in institutional services, or a combination of these factors. The possible implications for reimbursement and surgical training require direct study using linked patient-level, cost, tariff, and training data.
